data.title: Most AI value will come from broad automation, not from R & D
data.author: ydnyshhh
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了人工智能（AI）对未来经济的影响，特别是通过自动化研发（R&D）推动经济增长的观点。尽管一些业内有影响力的人士如Dario Amodei、Demis Hassabis和Sam Altman认为AI将主要通过加速R&D来产生经济效益，文章对此提出质疑。文章指出，R&D对经济增长的实际贡献小于普遍认知，且多数R&D成果无法被企业直接获利。此外，自动化R&D工作的难度高于预期，因为研究工作不仅涉及推理，还需要多种能力。因此，AI的经济价值更可能来自广泛的经济部署，而非仅限于R&D自动化。最终，文章认为AI的广泛应用将推动生产力提升和经济增长，但主要不是通过R&D渠道。

主要讨论点：科技乐观主义与技术进步对社会的影响

不同观点：
• [techpineapple] 认为科技乐观主义令人沮丧，原因有二：一是技术取代人性，二是过度炒作的技术难以实现，缺乏对社会的实际益处。
• [teleforce] 强调约束编程（CP）在解决数据驱动AI无法处理的任务中的潜力，并指出其被忽视的地位以及与AI领域重要人物的历史联系。
• [getnormality] 对文章中关于研发支出与生产力增长关系的论述持怀疑态度，认为其概念抽象且脱离实际。
• [mooreds] 引用一篇2015年的文章，讨论技术部署的重要性，并认为生成型AI仍在探索阶段，而机器学习（ML）已进入部署阶段。
• [bashfulpup] 批评简单与复杂任务自动化的二分法，指出即使简单的任务自动化也面临挑战，并提到RPA（机器人流程自动化）的局限性。
• [mirekrusin] 认为争论研发与一般自动化的受益先后并无意义，指出历史统计数据与当前技术突破的脱节。
• [mitjam] 讨论AI对人力劳动相对价值的影响，提出社会、文化与象征资本的重要性，并预测法规与团体思维可能增加。
• [stego-tech] 将当前自动化趋势比作工业与农业革命，认为广泛的劳动自动化将导致资本提升而非社会提升，除非工人采取行动争取利益分配。
• [KoolKat23] 同意文章观点，认为存在大量低成本高效益的自动化机会，如Excel VBA的普遍使用。
• [yellowapple] 认为AI最终将在经济价值活动中超越人类，但问题在于谁将受益，并提出四种可能的未来情景，从技术乐观主义承诺的乌托邦到反自动化 purges。
• [callamdelaney] 简单计算美国自动化市场的潜在规模，指出10%的工作自动化意味着1.2万亿美元的市场。
• [klooney] 指出美国主要从事研发与服务行业，生产自动化可能不被明显感受到。
• [coldtea] 认为大多数AI自动化将集中在无用的官僚工作上，而非实际生产力提升。
• [AndrewKemendo] 技术上赞同机器将取代人类劳动，尤其是在劳动效率为关键因素的领域，但指出仍未解决“谁将受益”的问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于技术进步的实际效益与社会影响，特别是自动化对就业市场与社会结构的冲击。
• 不同评论者对自动化技术成熟度与应用范围的看法存在分歧，一些人认为其潜力被过度炒作，另一些人则看到具体机会与挑战。
• 关于未来社会发展的预测，评论者们提出了多种可能性，从技术乌托邦到反乌托邦，反映了对此技术影响的复杂态度。

43447616.article_content:
A popular view about the future impact of AI on the economy is that it will be primarily mediated through AI automation of R&D. In some form or another, this view has been expressed by many influential figures in the industry:
In his essay
“Machines of Loving Grace”
, Dario Amodei lists five ways in which AI can benefit humanity in a scenario where AI goes well. He considers biology R&D, neuroscience R&D, and economics R&D as three of these ways. There’s no point at which he clearly argues that AI will lead to high rates of economic growth due to being broadly deployed throughout the economy as opposed to speeding up R&D and perhaps improving economic governance.
Demis Hassabis, CEO of DeepMind, is also bullish on R&D as the main channel through which AI will benefit society.
In a recent interview
, he provides specific mechanisms through which this could happen: AI could cure all diseases and “solve energy”. He mentions “radical abundance” as a possibility as well, but beyond the R&D channel doesn’t name any other way in which this could come about.
In his essay
“Three Observations”
, Sam Altman takes a more moderate position and explicitly says that in some ways AI might end up like the transistor, a big discovery that scales well and seeps into every corner of the economy. However, even he singles out the impact of AI on scientific progress as likely to “surpass everything else”.
Overall, this view is surprisingly influential despite not having been supported by any rigorous economic arguments. We’ll argue in this issue that it’s also very likely wrong.
R&D is generally not as economically valuable as people assume – increasing productivity and new technologies are certainly essential for long-run growth, but the contribution of explicit R&D to these processes is smaller than people generally think. Moreover, even most of this contribution is external and not captured in profits by the company performing the R&D, reducing the incentive to deploy systems to perform R&D in the first place. This combination means most AI systems will actually be deployed and earn revenue from tasks that are unrelated to R&D, and in aggregate these tasks will be more economically valuable as well.
It’s also significantly harder to automate R&D jobs than it might naively seem, because most tasks in the job of a researcher are not “reasoning tasks” and depend crucially on capabilities such as agency, multimodality, and long-context coherence. Once AI capabilities are already at a point where the job of a researcher can be entirely automated, it will also be feasible to automate most other jobs in the economy, which for the above reason would most likely create much more economic value than narrowly automating R&D alone.
When we combine these two points, there’s no reason to expect most of the economic value of AI to come from R&D at any point in the future. A much more plausible scenario is that the value of AI will be driven by broad economic deployment, and while we should expect this to
lead to an increase in productivity and output per person
due to increasing returns to scale, most of this increase will probably not come from explicit R&D.
Stay one step ahead
Get the latest from Gradient Updates in your inbox
Subscribe
The primary economic impact of AI will be its ability to
broadly
automate labor
There are two related but subtly different claims that we want to tease apart in this section, one we agree with and another we disagree with:
A technology that could automate R&D entirely, and was only used for this purpose, would be highly valuable and would likely add at least a few percentage points to economic growth per year.
We think this claim is true and it’s hard to argue against it.
In the real world, the most socially or economically valuable application of such a technology would in fact be to automate R&D.
This is the claim we will be disputing. While R&D is valuable, we don’t think it’s where we should expect most of the economic value or growth benefits from AI, both before and after AIs exceed human performance on all relevant tasks.
To understand our argument disputing the second claim, we must first measure the actual economic value of R&D. We know that R&D gets its economic value primarily through improving productivity, so to quantify the impact of R&D we might ask how much of the growth in labor productivity in the past has been due to R&D spending and its associated spillovers. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics
estimates that
R&D financed by private firms only accounted for around 0.2%/yr of total factor productivity (TFP) growth in the US from 1988 to 2022, compared to around 0.8%/yr of total TFP growth over the same period and around 1.9%/yr of labor productivity growth.
Though
public R&D spending
is only around a quarter of
total R&D spending
in the US economy, we might also expect it to have larger positive externalities, and

data.title: The belay test and the modern American climbing gym
data.author: vasco
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了攀岩天才彼得·梅菲尔德（Peter Mayfield）如何在美国创建首个盈利性室内攀岩馆的故事。20世纪80年代末，攀岩还是一项小众活动，而梅菲尔德在目睹欧洲的攀岩墙后，决心在美国开设类似的设施。他不仅想为专业攀岩者提供训练场所，更希望吸引儿童和企业活动，打造一个“室内攀岩学院”。尽管不被行业看好，梅菲尔德通过在一次攀登中结识投资者，成功筹集资金，并最终实现了他的梦想。他的创新理念改变了攀岩馆的运营模式，为现代攀岩馆的普及奠定了基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：攀岩馆文化、安全检查（belay test）的必要性、攀岩行业的历史与发展、技术与创新对攀岩的影响

不同观点：
• **关于belay test的争议**：
   - **mordechai9000**：认为belay test是必要的，因为即使是经验丰富的攀岩者也会在安全检查中失误，导致事故。举例说明一些老手因 complacency 而犯错，如国际运动员的教练在使用grigri时因分心导致攀爬者坠落。
   - **marsten**：回忆起90年代攀岩馆的早期发展，提到一些有经验的攀岩者如Peter在室内和户外攀岩中都非常出色，且belay test在当时并不普遍。

• **现代攀岩馆的便利性**：
   - **drcode**：提到现代攀岩馆使用autobelay设备，使得独自一人也可以安全攀爬，同时强调初学者仍需上课并通过belay test。
   - **dgfitz**：分享了一次因belayer失误而导致自己对绳索攀爬失去信任的经历，从此转向抱石攀岩。

• **攀岩行业的保守性与创新挑战**：
   - **thirtywatt**：指出攀岩行业对新技术和方法的抵制，市场依赖声誉和传统，创新者面临困难，行业内存在竞争和矛盾。
   
• **攀岩馆的历史和发展**：
   - **packetlost**：分享了其家族在90年代参与攀岩馆创业的历史，特别是在威斯康星州经营"The Barn"的经历，最终促成了Boulders Climbing Gym的成立。
   - **necubi**：提到Berkeley Ironworks的历史演变，指出其从City Rock继承而来，并与现代攀岩馆对比，认为其虽然老旧但仍有魅力。

• **个人攀岩经历与技术发展**：
   - **egl2020**：分享了自己在1970年通过belay test的经历，使用混凝土块和hip belay方法。
   - **Fricken**：描述了北美早期室内攀岩墙的发展，包括1989年在阿尔伯塔大学建立的Entreprises墙，以及当地攀岩者如何在天然场所训练。

补充讨论：
• **技术问题与用户体验**：
   - **exabrial**：抱怨网站视频播放器的技术问题，特别是无法轻松禁用JavaScript，影响了用户体验。

• **跨领域对比与联想**：
   - **CephalopodMD**：意识到室内攀岩起源于硅谷，解释了为何科技行业从业者与攀岩爱好者之间有高度重叠，不是个人心理因素，而是历史原因。
   - **MarcelOlsz**：提到Dan Iaboni在跑酷领域的类似创业经历，从社区自建场地到大型商业场馆的发展，鼓励对攀岩有兴趣的人也可以关注这一领域。

争议焦点：
• **belay test的必要性**：一些评论者认为belay test对于确保安全至关重要，而另一些评论者则通过个人经历指出即使通过测试的人也可能犯错，导致对绳索攀爬失去信心。

Peter Mayfield bouldering at City Rock
Photo: Peter Mayfield Collection

Download the app
.
Forty years ago, there was not a single purpose-built climbing gym in the U.S. In 1987, Seattle’s Vertical Club opened and a year later, the Portland Rock Gym launched. But the concept of a profitable indoor climbing gym was far from proven. This is the story of the person whose vision and determination would revolutionize climbing gyms as we know them today.
Peter Mayfield was a climbing prodigy. At 16 years old, in 1978, he was repeating the hardest free climbs in Yosemite. He went on to establish some of the hardest aid routes on the Valley’s big walls. By the age of 19, he was guiding for the prestigious Yosemite Mountaineering School, and became chief guide a year later. When sport climbing competitions began in the late 1980s, Mayfield participated in the first ever Snowbird climbing competition as well as Jeff Lowe’s national competitions.
In 1988, Mayfield formed a guiding cooperative with legends Kim Schmitz and
Jim Bridwell
, but by his mid-twenties, he was looking for a job that would keep him closer to home. So when Bridwell returned from a trip to Europe with posters and magazines of climbing walls going up in France, Mayfield knew he’d found his next venture.
Peter Mayfield at 19 years old on his first ascent in 1981 of Zenyatta Mondatta on El Cap with Jim Bridwell. Twenty years after his FA, Mayfield repeated the route with his 19-year-old son Braden. (Photo: Peter Mayfield Collection)
At the time, the walls in France were closer to artwork in public spaces than purpose-built climbing structures. It was around that time that the Vertical Club—a space for experienced climbers to train—went up, but Mayfield had something completely different in mind. As chief guide of the Yosemite Mountaineering School, he didn’t just want to create a place for himself and his buddies to get stronger. “I had this serious career of turning people onto this sport,” reflects Mayfield. “I was really thinking [about] kids, corporate programs … The word gym wasn’t even in my mind. It was more like an indoor climbing institute.”
With the popularity of
indoor climbing gyms
these days, it’s hard to imagine what it was like in the late ’80s, when climbing itself was still very much a niche activity. Mayfield knew that to keep the gym lights on, he’d need to attract more than just his hardcore climbing buddies.
Then there was the problem with California’s legendary great weather. Mayfield was skeptical that climbers would want to climb indoors on days when the sun was shining, because unlike Seattle and Portland, you could climb outdoors virtually year-round. So his marketing plan was also designed to get non-climbers to come to his gym. He wanted to build a place where “10,000 eight-year-old girls could try something they never dreamed of.”
“That was my pitch,” Mayfield says.
The economics of the first commercial climbing gym
Mayfield found his first investor while guiding an ascent of
Alaska’s Moose’s Tooth
. Tent-bound by storms for days, he discussed his climbing gym dreams with his clients. At the end of the expedition, as they were splitting up at the Oakland Airport, one of the clients asked him what he needed to start his business. He replied that he needed money for a phone line. The client pulled out his wallet and gave him $200. “I literally got handed two C-notes to start my business,” he remembers. He used that money to put in a Pacific Bell phone line in his mother’s basement in Berkeley and got to work.
“I got no positive reaction from the [climbing] industry at all,” remembers Mayfield. “I was pretty connected because I climbed with Bridwell. I met with the CEO of The North Face. I met with the CEO of Marmot. I met with the president of REI. They all said ‘it will never work. It makes sense in Seattle where it rains. Who would ever climb indoors in California?”
Mayfield even sent his business plan to Yvon Chouinard. “He was very polite and gave me some good advice,” Mayfield recalls. “He did not invest. None of them invested. But he kind of got what I was talking about.” (Chouinard did tell Mayfield that he should try to sell milkshakes: “If you can nail it with the youth, you will kick ass.”)
So Mayfield widened his net, contacting ”everybody in Silicon Valley who had ever climbed” and raised half a million dollars with 48 limited partners, essentially a large group of $5,000 investors. He stalled for a while, dealing with the mountain of paperwork associated with creating such a high volume of limited partnerships. But in the midst of his fundraising, he produced the Great Outdoor Adventure Fair in San Francisco. To promote his concept to the general public, he set up a portable climbing wall at the fair.    - **thirtywatt**：指出攀岩行业对新技术和方法的抵制，市场依赖声誉和传统，创新者面临困难，行业内存在竞争和矛盾。
   
• **攀岩馆的历史和发展**：
   - **packetlost**：分享了其家族在90年代参与攀岩馆创业的历史，特别是在威斯康星州经营"The Barn"的经历，最终促成了Boulders Climbing Gym的成立。
   - **necubi**：提到Berkeley Ironworks的历史演变，指出其从City Rock继承而来，并与现代攀岩馆对比，认为其虽然老旧但仍有魅力。

• **个人攀岩经历与技术发展**：
   - **egl2020**：分享了自己在1970年通过belay test的经历，使用混凝土块和hip belay方法。
   - **Fricken**：描述了北美早期室内攀岩墙的发展，包括1989年在阿尔伯塔大学建立的Entreprises墙，以及当地攀岩者如何在天然场所训练。

补充讨论：
• **技术问题与用户体验**：
   - **exabrial**：抱怨网站视频播放器的技术问题，特别是无法轻松禁用JavaScript，影响了用户体验。

• **跨领域对比与联想**：
   - **CephalopodMD**：意识到室内攀岩起源于硅谷，解释了为何科技行业从业者与攀岩爱好者之间有高度重叠，不是个人心理因素，而是历史原因。

争议焦点：
• **belay test的必要性**：一些评论者认为belay test对于确保安全至关重要，而另一些评论者则通过个人经历指出即使通过测试的人也可能犯错，导致对绳索攀爬失去信心。

data.title: Project Aardvark: reimagining AI weather prediction
data.author: bentobean
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在天气预测中的应用及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [rkagerer] 提出是否所有历史数据（如浮标、气象气球、气象站等）以及过去的天气模型预测都已被存储，以便AI算法可以在历史数据上运行并与现有方法进行性能对比。他还提到了是否存在一个集中的数据中心来存储这些数据。
• [eternityforest] 则关注AI是否能够通过普通消费级传感器或诸如摄像头、麦克风阵列等设备来进行本地天气预报。
• [jedberg] 指出，用于收集数据的资金被削减，这可能会影响数据的获取和天气预报的准确性，并提供了一篇相关文章的链接。
• [lenerdenator] 对模型的准确性提出了挑战，特别是在堪萨斯城地铁的天气预测中，两天以上的预测准确性较差。
• [timthorn] 提供了Richard Turner的一次演讲链接，讨论了AI天气预测的工作原理。
• [MostlyStable] 提出了一个假设，即未来的AGI代理是否能够像人类本能地预测球的飞行轨迹一样，本能地进行天气预测。
• [kgwgk] 提供了相关论文的链接。
• [herodoturtle] 提到了一个旧的FogCreek实习项目，并回忆了一部相关的纪录片。
• [bazzargh] 讨论了Turing Institute的历史，并提到过去的AI研究与现在的不同。
• [politelemon] 对模型如何取代数据收集步骤提出了疑问。
• [westoque] 提到其父亲在海洋微风和降雨模型方面的研究，并表示对AI和机器学习在天气预测中的进展感兴趣。
• [noiv] 提供了模型数据的链接。
• [dsr_] 指出文章中并未明确说明新模型的准确性是否能与当前最佳模型相媲美。
• [abdullahkhalids] 质疑在气候快速变化的背景下，过去的经验不再能预测未来，ML模型的鲁棒性如何。
• [interludead] 对模型如何处理飓风或罕见的极端天气事件等边缘情况表示关注。

补充讨论：
• 数据存储与访问：多个评论提到了历史数据存储和访问的重要性，包括是否存在一个集中的数据中心。
• 模型的准确性与性能对比：讨论了新AI模型与现有模型的性能对比，以及在不同天气情况下的预测准确性。
• 资金与资源问题：提到资金削减对数据收集和天气预报准确性的影响。
• 未来AI的发展：探讨了未来AGI代理在天气预测中的潜力及其与人类预测方式的类比。
• 极端天气事件的处理：对模型在处理罕见天气事件方面的能力表示关注。

data.title: The Vatican's Latinist (2017)
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了美国神父雷吉纳尔德·福斯特（Reginald Foster）的独特经历。1970年，他因出色的拉丁文才被梵蒂冈相中，尽管其上级芬尼亚·莫纳汉（Finian Monahan）反对，他还是被带入梵蒂冈负责教宗的拉丁文信件。福斯特在梵蒂冈工作了四十年，以其直率个性和非传统言论闻名，如“我喜欢裸体做弥撒”等言论曾引发争议。尽管如此，他作为拉丁文教师的影响力巨大，被誉为“过去半个世纪最具影响力的拉丁文教师”，其教学方法独特且具变革性。福斯特强调拉丁文作为人类交流的媒介，而非仅供学术分析。他的教学风格严厉，反对学术虚饰，注重实际语言掌握。他的职业生涯虽有波折，但其对拉丁文教育的贡献深远。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Reginald Foster及其拉丁语教学方法的评价与怀念，以及学习拉丁语的资源和方法

不同观点：
• [schoen] 认为Foster是一位出色的老师，他培养了许多仍在教授拉丁语的学生。文章未提到Foster在2020年去世。
• [dhosek] 分享了自己通过晚期拉丁语文本（如Beeson’s Primer of Medieval Latin和Vulgate Bible）重建拉丁语知识的经验，并表示虽然不会完全流利，但阅读能力已经相当扎实。
• [coolsunglasses] 强调Foster是反对传统语法教学法的代表人物，认为这种方法在多个领域尤其是教学法上造成了损失。现代真正能流利阅读、听懂或说拉丁语的人大多直接或间接受到Foster方法的影响。
• [spudlyo] 推荐了"Lingua Latina Per Se Illustrata"作为学习拉丁语的教材，并介绍了Legentibus应用，认为这些资源使得学习拉丁语变得更加容易和有趣。还提到了在线拉丁语学习社区的活跃性。

• 提供了丰富的学习资源链接和推荐，如[Koshkin]提供的早期印欧语言学习网站，[spudlyo]提到的Legentibus应用和Lingua Latina Per Se Illustrata教材。

43457202.article_content:
I
n
1970, the Procurator General of the Discalced Carmelite Order, Finian Monahan, was summoned to the Vatican for a meeting. The subject of the meeting was a promising young American priest by the name of Reginald Foster. The head Latinist of the Vatican’s State Department had tapped Foster to write papal correspondence, which was at the time composed entirely in Latin. Foster wanted the job but was bound by a vow of obedience, and the decision would be made by his superiors. Monahan intended to resist. Foster, thirty years of age, had proven himself to be both supremely intellectually gifted and utterly reliable—a precious thing at a time when the Catholic Church’s religious orders were hemorrhaging priests. Monahan thought Latin was a dead end. He didn’t want to lose one of his best to a Vatican department that would only get less and less important every year. He said Foster would go to the Vatican “over my dead body.”
Foster remembers the meeting vividly. “So we arrive there, and we’re ushered into this office, and who do we find there but Ioannes Benelli,” Foster says, using Benelli’s Latin name, as was customary at the Vatican at that time. He continues:
Benelli was Paul
VI
’s hatchet man—whenever he wanted something to get done, he called on Benelli. He was very energetic—got things done, and no nonsense. Everyone was terrified of him. I was too, and now here we were in the room with him, and he turns to Monahan and says, “This is Foster?” The General said yes. Then Benelli said, “Thank you very much, we won’t be needing you anymore.” And he took me by the hand and brought me down to the State Department and that was the end of that. Monahan didn’t say a word. I was now working for the Pope, and it was like I was more or less out of the Carmelite Order. A lot of the time the Order didn’t even really know what I was doing.
Foster would spend the next forty years at the Vatican, part of a small team of scribes who composed the pope’s correspondence, translated his encyclicals, and wrote copy for internal church documents. His somewhat unique position between the Carmelite Order and the Vatican bureaucracy meant that in fact he had a great deal of freedom for a priest. Later in his career his loose tongue—some in the church called it a loose cannon—would attract the notice of journalists looking for interesting copy. “Sacred language?” he said when asked about Latin as the “sacred language” of the church. “In the first century every prostitute in Rome spoke it fluently—and much better than most people in the Roman Curia.” The Minnesota
Star Tribune
quoted him as saying “I like to say mass in the nude,” which caused a small Curial kerfuffle (Foster claims he was misquoted). He appeared in Bill Maher’s movie
Religulous
, which featured him agreeing with the proposition that the Vatican itself was at odds with the message of Jesus, that the pope should not be living in a palace, and that hell and “that Old Catholic stuff” was “finished” and “gone.” Foster says the pope received complaints from bishops and cardinals about his appearance. “They said ‘Who is this Latinist of yours and what the hell is he doing?’ They would have fired me for sure. But by the time the film came out I was sick and a few months away from retirement anyway. So they just waited it out and let me go quietly.” He had already been fired from his post at the pontifical Gregorian University for allowing dozens of students to take his classes without paying for them.
B
es
ides being the Pope’s Latinist and “one of the Vatican’s most colorful characters” (as the Catholic News Service called him), Foster has been a tireless champion of Latin in the classroom. Indeed, Foster’s greatest legacy may be as a teacher. “The most influential Latin teacher in the last half-century is Reggie Foster,” says Dr. Nancy Llewellyn, professor of Latin at Wyoming Catholic College. “That’s not just my opinion—that’s a fact. For decades, he had the power to change lives like no other teacher in our field. I saw him for an hour in Rome in 1985 and that one hour completely changed my life. His approach was completely different from every other Latin teacher out there, and it was totally transformative.”
A humanist par excellence.
A humanist par excellence, Latin for Foster was not something to be dissected by linguistic analysis or serve as the raw data for a theory of gender or poetics: it was a language, a medium of human connection. I first met Foster in 1995, at his summer school, and couldn’t get enough: I returned seven times. No one on Earth was reading as much Latin as he and his students were, but he was more like an old-school newspaper editor than an academic: he wanted the
story
. But for that you actually had to know Latin, and know it well. Foster was ruthless about ignorance, and equally ruthless about anything that to him looked like mere academic posturing. “I don’t care about your garbage literary theory!” he barked at his students one day. “
43457202.article_summary: 本文讲述了美国神父雷吉纳尔德·福斯特（Reginald Foster）的独特经历。1970年，他因出色的拉丁文才被梵蒂冈相中，尽管其上级芬尼亚·莫纳汉（Finian Monahan）反对，他还是被带入梵蒂冈负责教宗的拉丁文信件。福斯特在梵蒂冈工作了四十年，以其直率个性和非传统言论闻名，如“我喜欢裸体做弥撒”等言论曾引发争议。尽管如此，他作为拉丁文教师的影响力巨大，被誉为“过去半个世纪最具影响力的拉丁文教师”，其教学方法独特且具变革性。福斯特强调拉丁文作为人类交流的媒介，而非仅供学术分析。他的教学风格严厉，反对学术虚饰，注重实际语言掌握。他的职业生涯虽有波折，但其对拉丁文教育的贡献深远。

data.title: How arrow-rs is able to decode JSON so fast
data.author: necubi
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Arroyo团队如何通过arrow-rs库实现高效的列式JSON解码。JSON是流处理管道中常用的序列化格式，但其解析过程往往占用大量CPU资源。为了提高性能，Arroyo使用基于Apache Arrow的列式内存格式，并扩展arrow-json以支持流式处理、原始JSON存储和无效数据处理。通过批量解码，Arroyo能将JSON文档转换为列数组，实现高效操作。与Flink使用的Jackson反序列化器相比，arrow-json在处理大型嵌套记录时速度提升了2.3倍。文章详细介绍了列构建、字符串和列表处理以及结构解码等技术细节，展示了如何通过优化JSON解码提升流处理引擎的速度。
data.comments_summary:

43454238.article_content:
Blog
Updates from the Arroyo team
Fast columnar JSON decoding with arrow-rs
February 25, 2025
JSON is the most common serialization format used in streaming pipelines, so it pays to be able to deserialize it fast. This post covers in detail how the arrow-json library works to perform very efficient columnar JSON decoding, and the additions we've made for streaming use cases.
Micah Wylde
CEO of Arroyo
My day job is working on the
Arroyo
stream processing engine, which executes complex, stateful queries over
high-scale streams of events. Computing things like windowed aggregates, stream
joins, and incrementally-computed SQL involves, as you might imagine, a lot of
sophisticated algorithms and systems. Doing it much faster than existing systems
like Apache Flink took careful performance engineering at every level of the
stack.
But…I'm going to let you in on a little secret. The sad truth of this industry,
which no one will tell you, is that so, so many data pipelines spend the bulk of their
CPU time…deserializing JSON
1
.
That's right. Everybody's favorite human-readable and sorta-human-writable data
interchange format has been responsible for >50% of CPU usage on several
high-scale Flink pipelines I've worked on. And so if you want to build a
fast stream processing engine, you need to start with a fast JSON
deserialization strategy
2
.
Arroyo's internal data representation is built on top of
Arrow
, a columnar in-memory format designed for
fast analytical processing
3
. So our challenge is to take row-oriented JSON;
parse it, and build out columns from the corresponding field in each
document. And do this as fast as possible.
Fortunately, we don't have to start from scratch: the
arrow-rs project
includes a very fast JSON
decoder, largely written by
Raphael Taylor-Davies
. I found the approach quite
interesting and thought it was worth writing up. So we'll dig into how
arrow-json works and then talk through Arroyo's extensions to support
raw
JSON
—leaving parts of the JSON serialized—and the ability to skip records in a
batch that don't match the schema. Along the way you should pick up some
intuition for how to work with columnar data, which many engineers find
challenging and unfamiliar in our typically row-oriented world.
Table of contents
But is this fast?
Batched decoding
Stealing from the best
Run the tape
Strings
Lists
An example

Struct decoding
Primitive and String decoding
Streaming extensions
Raw JSON
Invalid data handling
Wrapping up
But is this fast?
Before we get into the details, we might want to answer the question…is this
actually fast? And the answer is: yes! Benchmarking against the Jackson-based
deserializer used for Flink SQL, arrow-json is up to 2.3x faster:
Benchmark
Java (µs/record)
Rust (µs/record)
Speedup
Nexmark

(See
https://github.com/ArroyoSystems/json-benchmarks
for the benchmark source code and test documents.)
Arrow-json does particularly well with large, deeply nested records, and poorly
with enum-like structures where there are many null fields.
Batched decoding
Arrow, like other columnar formats, operates in
batches
. We're almost never
dealing with just one record (or “row”) of data, because columnar formats
achieve their high performance by storing many values together in a single
array. If you just have one row, the columnar overhead eats any performance
gains.
So our goal is to take a bunch of JSON documents (generally with a top-level
object) and turn them into a set of arrays representing each column of the
schema.
To make this concrete, let's take data representing HTTP server logs:

data.title: A proof checker meant for education
data.author: alabhyajindal
data.article_summary: Deduce是一个自动化证明检查工具，旨在教育中帮助学生：1. 轻松入门，证明程序的正确性；2. 加深对逻辑的理解；3. 提高撰写数学证明的能力。该工具通过自动化验证帮助学生更好地掌握逻辑和证明技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Deduce软件的评价和相关问题的讨论

不同观点：
• [iNic] 认为Deduce的语法比Lean更友好，可能非常不错，但对Deduce的Live Code环境有抱怨，提到在运行代码时遇到`undefined variable: Nat`错误，导致体验不佳。
• [krick] 对Deduce是否适合作为教育工具表示疑问，不确定是否应该用Deduce而不是Lean进行学习，并指出学习Lean有95%在于学习其库。同时，krick表示自己没有实际使用过类似工具。
• [angelaguilera] 关注Deduce使用的软件许可证问题，提到虽然网站声称是开源的，但在GitHub仓库中未找到许可证信息。
• [ratmice] 表示喜欢教育性的证明检查器，认为Deduce的语法看起来不错，但指出缺少类似头文件的功能来声明证明类型。
• [rendaw] 质疑Deduce作为教育用途证明检查器的定位，反问为什么它不能作为通用证明检查器使用。
• [vitalmixofntrnt] 基于Curry-Howard同构，询问Deduce是否有编译器可以将证明编译成机器代码，并支持可选的内联汇编。
• [Q6T46nT668w6i3m] 对Deduce表示期待，提到喜欢并通常推荐Daniel Velleman的“Proof Designer”，但听说对初学者来说可能过于晦涩。

补充讨论：
• iNic的具体问题集中在Deduce的Live Code环境中的错误提示，影响了使用体验。
• krick对学习Lean和Deduce的取舍提出了自己的看法，尤其强调了Lean库的重要性。
• angelaguilera对开源许可证的关注显示了对软件法律和合规性的重视。
• ratmice从历史使用经验出发，对Deduce的功能提出了具体建议，并与其他工具进行了比较。
• rendaw对Deduce作为教育工具的定位提出质疑，但没有深入展开。
• vitalmixofntrnt的问题涉及高级技术实现，特别是Curry-Howard同构的应用。
• Q6T46nT668w6i3m分享了对其他教育工具的看法，并提到初学者对某些工具的反馈。

争议焦点：
• Deduce作为教育工具的定位是否合理，以及它是否也能作为通用证明检查器使用。

43434503.article_content:
What is Deduce?
Deduce is an automated proof checker meant for use in education to help students:
Ease their way into proving the correctness of programs.
Deepening their understanding of logic.
Improve their ability to write mathematical proofs.

data.title: Osgint – OSINT tool to find information about GitHub user
data.author: CHEF-KOCH
data.article_summary: OSGINT是一个开源工具，用于查找GitHub用户的各类信息。其主要功能包括：通过电子邮件查找GitHub用户名，通过用户名查找关联电子邮件（但并非每次都有效），以及获取用户资料信息（如账户创建日期、公开Gists、ID、公开PGP和SSH等）。该工具通过分析公开提交记录和GPG密钥来获取电子邮件信息，并利用GitHub的用户API进行数据检索。用户可以通过命令行指定用户名或电子邮件进行查询，并可以选择以JSON格式输出结果。工具还提供了示例输出，展示了查询结果的详细信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub 信息泄露及隐私问题，尤其是电子邮件地址的暴露，以及相关工具和用途的争议。

不同观点：
• **zellyn**：认为个人资料中的电子邮件信息可能不准确，提到有些邮件地址是他人提交代码时使用的。
• **Xaena**：指出该仓库的意图可能违反GitHub的可接受使用政策，特别是如果用于招聘或垃圾邮件目的，依据GitHub的隐私政策是可以举报的。
• **gokayburuc_dev**：质疑该功能是否必要，因为GitHub的API工具已经提供了类似的信息，并且大多数数据可以通过JSON格式免费获取。
• **cdblades**：认为有道德义务在README中加入如何避免信息泄露的说明，以保护用户隐私。
• **theyknowitsxmas**：质疑该工具的受益者，认为除了垃圾邮件发送者外，其他人不会从中受益。
• **1317**：认为该工具没有提供新的信息，除了电子邮件外，其他信息已经在GitHub的个人资料页面上公开。
• **ExxKA**：提到该工具可能为刚刚停止通过GitHub发送垃圾邮件的招聘人员提供了新的渠道。
• **cpursley**：指出该工具类似于https://reporeach.com，表明类似功能已经存在。
• **danso**：提供了技术上的建议，可以通过GitHub的Events API更高效地获取某人的最近提交和电子邮件信息。
• **Dotnaught**：认为这种方法比直接在提交后添加`.patch`要麻烦。
• **belter**：质疑谁会使用真实姓名注册GitHub，并给出了知名人物的例子（如Elon Musk和Donald Trump）。
• **areyourllySorry**：提到另一个类似工具“gitrecon”，表明类似功能和工具已经在开发者社区中存在。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于该工具是否会助长垃圾邮件行为，以及是否违反GitHub的隐私政策。
- 讨论中涉及了如何避免信息泄露以及保护个人隐私的技术和道德问题。
- 用户对于类似功能是否必要以及是否已有其他工具可以实现相同目的存在分歧。

data.title: Rickover's Lessons
data.author: pepys
data.article_summary: 文章总结了查尔斯·杨对美国工业政策的分析，重点介绍了海曼·里科弗上将如何通过建立核海军，推动美国在战略竞争中取得优势。文章指出，美国目前面临工业基础投资不足的问题，生产能力远不及中国，特别是在造船业和关键矿物加工方面。为应对挑战，美国需要从里科弗的成功经验中学习，他通过强有力的领导和技术创新，在短时间内成功打造了世界首艘核潜艇和核动力航母，确保了美国在20世纪的海上战略优势。里科弗注重人才选拔与持续培训，亲自面试每一位候选人，并要求他们进行深入的自学和实地考察，以确保技术专精。文章最后强调，工业政策不仅依赖立法，更需要像里科弗这样的领导力和技术培训体系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对美国海军上将Hyman Rickover的管理风格、成就及其现代应用的评价和争议

不同观点：
• **对Rickover管理风格的肯定与质疑**：
   - 一些人赞赏Rickover的严格管理和对细节的关注，认为这种风格确保了高质量的结果，尤其是在复杂的工程项目中（如核潜艇的建造和运行）。
   - 另一些人则认为他的管理风格过于苛刻，可能不适合现代职场文化，尤其是千禧一代和Z世代的工程师。有人质疑现代公司是否能接受如此严厉的管理方式。

• **Rickover的成就与现代应用的反思**：
   - 有人指出Rickover的理念和方法对现代技术公司仍有借鉴意义，尤其是在培训和责任制方面。强调了理解基本原理和持续培训的重要性。
   - 然而，也有人认为现代公司过度依赖“无责文化”，导致问题无法有效解决，并指出Rickover式的严格要求可能提供了一种平衡，但需要找到适应当代的工作方式。

• **Rickover对美国海军和核工程的长期影响**：
   - Rickover的领导和核潜艇项目对美国海军和战略武器发展产生了深远的影响，但有人质疑当前美国潜艇建造行业是否真正继承了他的经验和教训。
   - 评论中提到澳大利亚在购买美国潜艇过程中遇到的问题，反映出美国潜艇建造行业可能未能保持Rickover时代的标准。

补充讨论：
• **Rickover的个性与管理哲学**：
   - Rickover以不追求“最佳”而追求潜力开发著称，他通过严格筛选和培训来塑造有能力的人才，而不是仅仅依赖“最优秀”的招聘口号。
   - 评论中有人将他与现代咨询公司（如麦肯锡）对比，指出过度强调“最佳”反而可能反映出不安全感。

• **历史与现实的对比**：
   - 一些评论者提到Rickover可能在职位上待得过久，暗示他的影响力可能在后期有所减弱。
   - 另一条评论通过分享Rickover的逸事（如摔设备测试耐用性）来展示他的实际作风，强调他对实际结果的重视。

争议焦点：
• Rickover管理风格的适用性：在现代职场中，尤其是面对新一代工程师时，Rickover式的严格管理是否仍然可行和有效。
• 美国潜艇建造行业的现状：是否真正继承了Rickover的遗产，以及澳大利亚购买美国潜艇过程中遇到的不公待遇。

总的来说，评论中对Rickover的评价褒贬不一，既肯定了他的成就和理念，也对其管理风格的现代适用性提出了质疑。

Charles Yang is the executive director for the
Center for Industrial Strategy
, a bipartisan think tank focused on industrial policy. Previously, he served as an AI and Supply Chain Policy Advisor at the Department of Energy and was an ML Engineer at an AI hardware startup in San Francisco. Today, he’s here to present some excerpts from
his research
into how Admiral Hyman Rickover built the nuclear navy.
Strategic competition demands more than technological innovation — it requires building industrial power. The U.S. is realizing the damage done by decades of underinvestment in the nation’s industrial base, which now jeopardizes its ability to compete on the global stage. Today, the production capacity of
Chinese shipyards is over 200 times that of US shipyards
, and China has used its
chokehold on critical mineral processing as leverage
to retaliate against US sanctions.
A new bipartisan consensus is emerging around the need for industrial policy — from the passage of the CHIPS and Science Act, to the recent bipartisan introduction of the
SHIPS for America Act
and the
Critical Minerals for the Future Act
.
As Congress steps into this more active role, policymakers should learn from the successes of our past. Nearly 75 years ago, Admiral Hyman G. Rickover, “Father of the Nuclear Navy”, pioneered a bold program to develop and operationalize nuclear power in the Navy. Under his leadership, the U.S. government harnessed the power of the atom, building the world’s first nuclear-powered submarine and the world’s largest fleet of nuclear reactors for civilian power.
Lessons From the Past
Rickover spent his entire career in the Navy and is still the longest-serving naval officer in US history. He spent the first 20 years of his career as an electrical engineer, where he honed a strong technical foundation and unique management style. In 1946, he was assigned a 1-year tour of duty at the Oak Ridge site of the Manhattan Project. Rickover immediately recognized the transformative potential of nuclear technology — he spent the rest of his career building the “Nuclear Navy,” which ensured US strategic dominance of the high seas for the rest of the 20th century.
Within the span of 10 years, Rickover created an entire office dedicated to nuclear propulsion, and successfully launched the world’s first nuclear-powered submarine without cost overruns. He conclusively demonstrated the strategic importance of nuclear propulsion in a timeframe no one thought possible and helped the US beat the Soviets to nuclear propulsion for submarines by 3 years. His institutional legacy is the US Navy’s safe construction and operation of nuclear reactors.
As the US gears up for another strategic competition, Rickover’s story can offer helpful lessons for aspiring technocrats. Oftentimes, industrial policy is framed in terms of legislation, but Rickover demonstrates that industrial policy is as much about policy as it is about strong leadership.
USS Enterprise, the world’s first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier.
Source
.
Talent, Training, and Management
Rickover spent an inordinate amount of time focused on interviewing personnel —
he made the final hiring decision for every naval officer who applied to serve on a nuclear submarine until he retired
. And he was an unorthodox interviewer, screening for high agency individuals who could think on their feet — literally! To test their composure, Rickover famously made candidates sit in a chair with the front two legs shortened as he loomed over them during questioning.
The infamous “Rickover chair”
One interview account:
For one interviewee who said he liked hiking, Rickover asked him if he had ever hiked the nearby “Goat Mountain”. When he said he had not, Rickover told him to bring him proof he had climbed it by tomorrow morning and he would be hired. It turns out that Goat Mountain was the peak of a structure for mountain goats in a zoo. He went to the zoo, asked a tourist to take his picture, jumped into the enclosure, and climbed to the top. He’s hired the next day!
But it didn’t end at the interview process — Rickover believed in continued technical training for his staff and in building out a talented workforce base for this new technology:
While Rickover worked to staff up quickly in the short term, he also set out to build a deep bench and a long-term pipeline of talent. He required each officer and engineer he hired to submit a self-study plan demonstrating mastery of advanced texts in metallurgy, physics, and chemistry, along with field trips to AEC facilities, totaling 854 hours of study or 16 hours per week. He also worked with MIT to develop a survey course on nuclear physics and a master's degree in nuclear engineering,

   - Rickover的领导和核潜艇项目对美国海军和战略武器发展产生了深远的影响，但有人质疑当前美国潜艇建造行业是否真正继承了他的经验和教训。
   - 评论中提到澳大利亚在购买美国潜艇过程中遇到的问题，反映出美国潜艇建造行业可能未能保持Rickover时代的标准。

补充讨论：
• **Rickover的个性与管理哲学**：
   - Rickover以不追求“最佳”而追求潜力开发著称，他通过严格筛选和培训来塑造有能力的人才，而不是仅仅依赖“最优秀”的招聘口号。
   - 评论中有人将他与现代咨询公司（如麦肯锡）对比，指出过度强调“最佳”反而可能反映出不安全感。

• **历史与现实的对比**：
   - 一些评论者提到Rickover可能在职位上待得过久，暗示他的影响力可能在后期有所减弱。
   - 另一条评论通过分享Rickover的逸事（如摔设备测试耐用性）来展示他的实际作风，强调他对实际结果的重视。

争议焦点：
• Rickover管理风格的适用性：在现代职场中，尤其是面对新一代工程师时，Rickover式的严格管理是否仍然可行和有效。
• 美国潜艇建造行业的现状：是否真正继承了Rickover的遗产，以及澳大利亚购买美国潜艇过程中遇到的不公待遇。

总的来说，评论中对Rickover的评价褒贬不一，既肯定了他的成就和理念，也对其管理风格的现代适用性提出了质疑。

data.title: Researchers search for more precise ways to measure pain
data.author: Petiver
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：疼痛的主观性、测量方法及其在医疗实践中的应用

不同观点：
• j_bum认为疼痛包含感觉辨别和情感情绪两个主要成分，且两者可以独立或同时发生。他质疑情感情绪成分的生物标志物是否可靠，担心依赖生物标志物会使医生更加怀疑患者的疼痛体验，尤其是那些主要经历情感情绪疼痛的患者。他提到女性和少数群体在疼痛信任方面面临更大的问题。
• pugworthy分享了自己在心脏病发作时被多次要求用1-10来评价疼痛的经历，认为这种方法可能不够准确，因为患者可能会随意给出数字。
• GarnetFloride强调急性和慢性疼痛的管理差异，并指出性别和种族可能影响医生对疼痛的认真程度。他提到描述疼痛对生活的影响比用数字评价更有效。
• PaulKeeble指出，研究显示使用6作为疼痛评分可以提高获得医疗帮助的机会，因为低于6的评分往往不被重视。他还提到慢性疼痛患者在缺乏生物标志物和阿片类药物撤回的情况下难以获得缓解。
• gaoshan提到文化差异可能导致疼痛描述的误解，例如用“酸”来描述疼痛在中文中是常见的，但在英语中可能不被理解。
• shadowtree强调疼痛的时间轴（持续时间和一致性）在评估中的重要性，认为慢性疼痛的螺旋效应难以理解和处理。
• lijok认为准确的疼痛测量机制在兽医学中也非常需要，因为动物的疼痛评估往往更加困难，导致许多动物在不确定是否真正痛苦的情况下被安乐死。
• failrate和INTPenis以幽默的方式讨论了疼痛描述和未来科技可能带来的解决方案，例如用机器感受患者的疼痛。
• _DeadFred_反思了疼痛测量在实际生活中的应用，提到即使有了测量工具，人们的反应可能仍然是漠不关心的。
• m3kw9认为疼痛是相对的，心理因素可以放大疼痛感受，例如对针头的恐惧会使疼痛感觉更强烈。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到性别和种族对疼痛评估的影响，特别是女性和少数群体在疼痛信任方面面临的挑战。
• 文化差异在疼痛描述中的作用也被提及，说明疼痛的主观性不仅限于个人体验，还可能受到语言和文化的影响。
• 对未来科技在疼痛测量中的应用充满期待，但也有人担心这些工具可能带来的新问题，例如对患者疼痛体验的误解或忽视。
• 兽医学中的疼痛评估被认为是一个亟待解决的问题，强调了疼痛测量在不同领域中的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该依赖生物标志物来测量疼痛，特别是对于情感情绪成分的疼痛。
• 用1-10的评分系统是否能够准确反映患者的疼痛体验，以及是否有更好的方法来评估疼痛。

data.title: Mastering Delphi 5 2025 Annotated Edition Is Now Complete
data.author: mariuz
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Delphi的历史、现状及其在编程领域的地位和影响

不同观点：
• FeistySkink认为，Delphi与VB6和WinForms一起，代表了UI开发的巅峰，而之后的开发工具，特别是在 web 开发方面，变得复杂且依赖繁多，导致环境配置和项目移植困难。
• WillAdams提问Lazarus IDE是否也属于类似的情况，暗示可能存在其他延续Delphi精神的现代工具。
• Kopirgan指出Borland（Delphi的开发公司）曾是行业先锋，但未能抵挡微软的竞争，最终在市场和策略上失败。
• Earth-adventure表达了对Delphi的个人情感，提到Delphi和相关书籍激励了自己进入编程领域。
• Lwn分享了对Delphi IDE的美好回忆，并提到不好的记忆逐渐淡去。
• Visarga表示虽然喜欢Delphi 1，但不会为了一种编程语言支付高额费用。
• CodeCompost提到Delphi社区的不友好经历，促使自己的公司转向C#。
• Markus_zhang好奇Delphi是否能在Windows 10/11上运行，并认为它仍可用于个人项目。
• Mikewarot期待将Delphi资源用作Lazarus的文档补充。

补充讨论：
• Theamk对博文提到的"Delphi 5"是否是1999年发布的Borland Delphi 5版本表示疑问，关注具体版本和功能。
• Havoc分享了对Delphi 5的正面评价，并指出Delphi 6在跳转定义功能上有所退步。
• Pjmlp和Michael-ax对Marco（可能是博主或作者）表示感谢，但没有提出具体观点或讨论。

争议焦点：
• Delphi是否真的比现代Web开发工具更易用，特别是在UI开发方面。
• 对Delphi社区的评价存在分歧，有人感激其贡献，有人因社区经历转向其他语言。

主要讨论点：DryStructs是否是一个有效的用于实现命名变量、类型验证和代码文档化的工具

不同观点：
• **支持DryStructs的观点**：
   - DryStructs提供命名变量、类型验证以及更好的代码文档，有助于提高代码的可读性和可维护性。
   - 通过DryStructs，代码结构更加清晰，类型验证功能可以减少运行时错误。
   - 提供了参考链接（https://dry-rb.org/gems/dry-struct/1.6/）以展示DryStructs的具体功能和使用方法。

• **可能的反对或担忧观点**：
   - 没有明确反对意见，但潜在担忧可能包括引入额外依赖（如DryStructs gem）是否会增加项目的复杂性，尤其是对于小型项目或团队不熟悉该工具的情况下。
   - 虽然DryStructs提供类型验证，但某些开发者可能认为手动类型检查或使用其他内置语言功能也能达到类似效果，从而不一定需要额外工具。

补充讨论：
• **工具的适用性**：
   - DryStructs在特定场景下（如需要大量数据结构和类型验证的项目中）可能非常有用，但对于小型或简单项目，其优势可能不明显。
   - 讨论中提到了具体使用案例（在之前的角色中使用过DryStructs），为该工具的实际应用提供了实际例子。

• **技术选择的多样性**：
   - 讨论暗示了在实现命名变量和类型验证方面，可能存在多种技术选择，DryStructs只是其中之一。
   - 开发者可能会基于项目需求、团队熟悉程度以及维护成本等因素选择不同的工具或方法。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点可能在于DryStructs是否为实现类型验证和命名变量的最佳工具，尤其是在权衡引入额外依赖与手动实现类似功能之间的取舍时。

data.title: Mruby/C and picoruby: high level langs in low-level devices?
data.author: rahil627
data.article_summary: PicoRuby 是一个专为单片微控制器设计的微型 Ruby 实现，具有小尺寸和可移植性特点。它在 32 位架构下仅需 256 KB ROM 和 128 KB 或更少的 RAM。PicoRuby 依赖标准 C 库，如 glibc 或 Newlib，并支持 Raspberry Pi Pico 等微控制器板。它提供了 API 文档和演示视频，并依赖于 mruby/c 实现的虚拟机。PicoRuby 可用于构建 PRK Firmware 键盘固件和 PicoRuby WASI WebAssembly 运行时。构建过程需要 C 工具链、git 和 Ruby 3.0 以上版本。项目仍在开发中，遵循 MIT 许可协议，并获得了 Ruby Association Grant Program 的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微控制器上不同编程语言和工具的适用性及优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持MicroPython**：[throwaway81523] 认为MicroPython非常流行，适合在能支持它的设备上使用，尤其是像Adafruit Trinket这样具有256KB闪存和32KB RAM的设备。虽然MicroPython在只有16KB RAM的BBC micro:bit上运行比较困难，但在多数小型设备上表现良好。另外，提到Lua和Hedgehog Lisp作为更小的选择，以及Javacard和J2ME在特定设备上的使用。对于极小设备，建议放弃垃圾回收机制，使用Forth或交叉编译语言。

• **MicroPython与C的结合**：[jononor] 喜欢MicroPython，并指出它易于与C语言结合使用，这对于在微控制器设备上获得最佳性能非常必要。

• **支持picoruby**：[aidog] 推荐picoruby，认为它非常有趣，是mruby/c的更小版本。他还分享了HASUMI Hitoshi的演示视频，展示了picoruby在Raspberry Pi Pico及其他微控制器上的应用。

• **支持高层次语言在微控制器上运行**：[calebh] 介绍了Juniper，一种用于Arduino的功能反应式编程语言，证明了高层次代码（如闭包）也可以在小型设备上运行。

• **提供picoruby的资源**：[xutopia] 提供了picoruby的文档链接，供感兴趣的人查阅。

• **再次推荐MicroPython**：[TkTech] 提到MicroPython在这个领域占据主导地位，并提供了GitHub链接供进一步了解。

• **对C语言的争议**：[rahil627] 提到有些人不喜欢使用C语言，而有些人则喜欢并拥抱它。同时提出疑问，Ruby这样的复杂语言在微控制器（如传感器）上是否有意义，并表示对pico上Ruby实现的维护感到欣赏。

• **提到Shedskin Python到C++编译器**：[actionfromafar] 提到了Shedskin，一个Python到C++编译器，作为另一种选择。

• **对设备存储的看法**：[bsder] 认为256KB闪存和128KB RAM已经不算小，比1990年之前的平均计算机还大，并指出RAM和闪存的大小对微控制器的价格有很大影响。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多种语言和工具，如MicroPython、picoruby、Lua、Hedgehog Lisp、Forth、Juniper、Javacard和J2ME，反映了在微控制器上运行不同类型语言的可行性和实用性。

43451760.article_summary: PicoRuby 是一个专为单片微控制器设计的微型 Ruby 实现，具有小尺寸和可移植性特点。它在 32 位架构下仅需 256 KB ROM 和 128 KB 或更少的 RAM。PicoRuby 依赖标准 C 库，如 glibc 或 Newlib，并支持 Raspberry Pi Pico 等微控制器板。它提供了 API 文档和演示视频，并依赖于 mruby/c 实现的虚拟机。PicoRuby 可用于构建 PRK Firmware 键盘固件和 PicoRuby WASI WebAssembly 运行时。构建过程需要 C 工具链、git 和 Ruby 3.0 以上版本。项目仍在开发中，遵循 MIT 许可协议，并获得了 Ruby Association Grant Program 的支持。

data.title: Thinking Different, Thinking Slowly: LLMs on a PowerPC Mac
data.author: tambourine_man
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者在2005年款PowerBook G4上成功运行大型语言模型（LLM）推理的实验过程。这台老式硬件配备1.5GHz处理器、1GB内存和32位地址空间。作者借鉴了Andrej Karpathy的llama2.c项目，通过C语言实现了Llama2模型的推理，并对其进行改进，创建了名为"ullm"的项目。作者对代码进行了多项优化，包括改进系统函数的封装、引入状态返回机制、组织成库结构并提供公开API以支持单元测试。最终，通过回调函数处理输出，实现了对整个推理流程的集成测试，成功让老旧硬件运行现代AI模型。

data.article_summary:
文章介绍了Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct模型，这是基于之前Qwen2.5-VL系列的优化版本。该模型具有以下特点：

1. **更符合人类偏好**：调整输出风格，提供更详细、格式更好的答案。
2. **数学推理能力显著提升**：解决复杂数学问题的准确性提高。
3. **细粒度图像理解和推理**：在图像解析、内容识别和视觉逻辑推理等方面精度和分析能力增强。

在性能对比中，Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct在多模态任务和纯文本能力上均表现优异，超越了包括Mistral-Small-3.1-24B和Gemma-3-27B-IT在内的多个同类模型，甚至在某些方面超过了更大的Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct。

文章还提供了几个演示案例，展示了模型在处理实际问题时的详细步骤和逻辑推理能力，如计算行车时间和解决几何角度问题。

QWEN CHAT

Introduction
#
At the end of January this year, we launched the Qwen2.5-VL series of models, which received widespread attention and positive feedback from the community. Building on the Qwen2.5-VL series, we continued to optimize the model using reinforcement learning and open-sourced the new VL model with the beloved 32B parameter scale under the Apache 2.0 license —
Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct
. Compared to the previously released Qwen2.5-VL series models, the features of this 32B VL model are as follows:
Responses More Aligned with Human Preferences
: Adjusted the output style to provide more detailed, better-formatted answers that align more closely with human preferences.
Mathematical Reasoning
: Significant improvement in the accuracy of solving complex mathematical problems.
Fine-grained Image Understanding and Reasoning
: Enhanced accuracy and detailed analysis in tasks such as image parsing, content recognition, and visual logic deduction.
Performance
#
Extensive benchmarking against state-of-the-art (SoTA) models of comparable scale,
Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct
has demonstrated superiority over baselines, e.g., Mistral-Small-3.1-24B and Gemma-3-27B-IT, even surpassing the larger
Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct
. Notably, it achieves significant advantages in multimodal tasks such as
MMMU
,
MMMU-Pro
, and
MathVista
, which focus on complex, multi-step reasoning. On
MM-MT-Bench
, a benchmark emphasizing subjective user experience evaluation,
Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct
outperforms its predecessor
Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct
by a substantial margin.
In addition to excelling in visual capabilities, Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct has also achieved top-tier performance in pure text capabilities at the same scale.
Demo Cases
#
Fine-grained Image Understanding and Reasoning
Next
User
I am driving a large truck on this road, and it is now 12 o’clock. Can I reach a place 110 kilometers away before 13 o’clock?
Qwen2.5-VL-32B
To determine whether you can reach a place 110 kilometers away before 13:00, we need to analyze the information provided:
Current Time
: It is 12:00.
Distance to Destination
: 110 kilometers.
Speed Limit for Trucks
: The speed limit sign indicates that the maximum speed for trucks is
100 km/h
.
Step-by-Step Analysis:
#
1.
Calculate the Required Travel Time
#
The formula to calculate travel time is:
\[
\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}}
\]
Given:
Distance = 110 km
Maximum Speed = 100 km/h
Substitute the values:
\[
\text{Time} = \frac{110 \text{ km}}{100 \text{ km/h}} = 1.1 \text{ hours}
\]
2.
Convert Time to Hours and Minutes
#
1.1 hours is equivalent to:
\[
1 \text{ hour} + 0.1 \times 60 \text{ minutes} = 1 \text{ hour} + 6 \text{ minutes} = 1 \text{ hour and } 6 \text{ minutes}
\]
3.
Determine Arrival Time
#
If you start at 12:00 and it takes 1 hour and 6 minutes to travel 110 kilometers, your arrival time will be:
\[
12:00 + 1 \text{ hour and } 6 \text{ minutes} = 13:06
\]
4.
Compare with Target Time
#
You want to arrive before 13:00. However, based on the calculations, you will arrive at 13:06, which is
after
13:00.
Conclusion:
#
Given the speed limit of 100 km/h for trucks, it is
not possible
to reach a place 110 kilometers away before 13:00.
Thus, the final answer is:
\[
\boxed{\text{No}}
\]
Mathematical Reasoning
Next
User
As shown in the figure, the straight lines AB and CD intersect at point O, OD bisects ∠AOE, ∠BOC = 50.0, then ∠EOB = ()
Qwen2.5-VL-32B
Problem Analysis
#
We are given the following information:
Straight lines $ AB $ and $ CD $ intersect at point $ O $.
$ OD $ bisects $ \angle AOE $.
$ \angle BOC = 50^\circ $.
We need to find $ \angle EOB $.
Step-by-Step Solution
#
Step 1: Understand the given information and relationships
#
Since $ AB $ and $ CD $ are straight lines intersecting at $ O $, the angles around point $ O $ sum up to $ 360^\circ $.
The vertically opposite angles are equal. Therefore:
$$
\angle AOD = \angle BOC \quad \text{and} \quad \angle DOB = \angle COA.
$$
Given $ \angle BOC = 50^\circ $, we have:
$$
\angle AOD = 50^\circ.
$$
Step 2: Use the angle bisector property
#
It is given that $ OD $ bisects $ \angle AOE $. This means:
$$
\angle AOD = \angle DOE.
$$
Since $ \angle AOD = 50^\circ $, we have:
$$
\angle DOE = 50^\circ.
$$
Step 3: Determine $ \angle AOE $
#
The angle $ \angle AOE $ is the sum of $ \angle AOD $ and $ \angle DOE $:
$$
\angle AOE = \angle AOD + \angle DOE = 50^\circ + 50^\circ = 100^\circ.
$$
Step 4: Use the straight line property
#
Since $ AB $ is a straight line, the angles on a straight line sum up to $ 180^\circ $. Therefore:
$$
\angle AOE + \angle EOB = 180^\circ.
$$
Substituting $ \angle AOE = 100^\circ $, we get:
$$
100^\circ + \angle EOB = 180^\circ.
$$
Solving for $ \angle EOB $:
$$
\angle EOB = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ.
$$
Final Answer
#
$$
\boxed{80}
$$

data.title: The Prospero Challenge
data.author: jstanley
data.article_summary:
《The Prospero Challenge》一文介绍了如何通过解析包含数学表达式的文本文件（prospero.vm）生成图像的挑战。该文件包含7866个数学表达式，通过计算(x,y)值并根据符号决定像素颜色，可以生成特定图像。挑战目标是以最快速度渲染出该图像。文章提供了一个基本的Python渲染器示例，利用Numpy实现像素并行处理，但该方法需要大量内存且耗时较长。

文章鼓励进一步优化，如预解析表达式、使用numba或GPU加速等。此外，还提出了多个优化思路和问题，如优化解释器或编译器设计、数学结构利用、图像大小与渲染时间的关系、以及交互式查看模型的策略等。

文章欢迎大家提交实验结果，并提供了提交方式和背景材料，以鼓励探索不同解决方案。虽然挑战没有丰厚奖励，但作者承诺对有趣的提交者在同城请喝咖啡。

43458780.article_content:
The Prospero Challenge
Matt Keeter
, March 2025
prospero.vm
is a plain-text file containing 7866 math expressions.
It begins as follows:
# Text of a monologue from The Tempest
_0 const 2.95
_1 var-x
_2 const 8.13008
_3 mul _1 _2
_4 add _0 _3
...and continues in that vein for many,
many
lines.
If you evaluate the expression with
(x,y)
values in the Â±1
square, then color pixels black or white based on their sign, you get the
following image:
The "challenge" is simple: render the image as quickly as possible.
A basic renderer is 28 lines of Python, using Numpy for pixel parallelism:
import numpy as np
with open('prospero.vm') as f:
text = f.read().strip()
image_size = 1024
space = np.linspace(-1, 1, image_size)
(x, y) = np.meshgrid(space, -space)
v = {}
for line in text.split('\n'):
if line.startswith('#'):
continue
[out, op, *args] = line.split()
match op:
case "var-x": v[out] = x
case "var-y": v[out] = y
case "const": v[out] = float(args[0])
case "add": v[out] = v[args[0]] + v[args[1]]
case "sub": v[out] = v[args[0]] - v[args[1]]
case "mul": v[out] = v[args[0]] * v[args[1]]
case "max": v[out] = np.maximum(v[args[0]], v[args[1]])
case "min": v[out] = np.minimum(v[args[0]], v[args[1]])
case "neg": v[out] = -v[args[0]]
case "square": v[out] = v[args[0]] * v[args[0]]
case "sqrt": v[out] = np.sqrt(v[args[0]])
case _: raise Exception(f"unknown opcode '{op}'")
out = v[out]
with open('out.ppm', 'wb') as f: # write the image out
f.write(f'P5\n{image_size} {image_size}\n255\n'.encode())
f.write(((out < 0) * 255).astype(np.uint8).tobytes())
On my machine, this takes about
15 seconds
to produce a 1024Ã1024 image.
(
Spoilers:
it also allocates 60+ GB of RAM for intermediate
results, so consider reducing the image size before running it on your own
machine)
"But wait!", you say.  "There's so much obvious room for improvement!  You
could pre-parse the expression, or use
numba
, or run it on
the GPU, or use LLVM ..."
Yes.
I would like you to do those things, and then tell me about
them!
This page has been seeded with a few of my projects, but I'd like for
it to grow to contain different experiments by other people.
A few ideas to think about:
The Python implementation above is a simple interpreter.  What would
an optimized interpreter look like?  How about a compiler?
How can we take advantage of the expression's mathematical
structure?
Start-up time versus steady-state performance.  What kinds of
precomputation help, and how long does it take?  (Obviously, you
could precompute the entire image, but that's against the spirit of
the challenge)
Along those lines, what happens if the user is making changes to the
model?  Strategies which rely on expensive precomputation may not be
suitable for interactive use.
How does rendering performance change with image size?  A 1024Ã1024
image has 4Ã as many pixels as 512Ã512; does it necessarily
take 4Ã longer to render?
Panning and zooming is a simple transform of the incoming
(x,y)
coordinates.  How does your system handle
interactive viewing of the model?
Submitting your experiments
Feel free to submit both successful and unsuccessful experiments via
email to
matt.j.keeter@gmail.com
,
and I will add them to this page.
The ideal submission would be a blog post or code repository, along
with a few-sentence description that you'd like included on this page.  I'd
also be happy to include hero images or video embeds.
The description should call out any particularly promising results,
clever ideas, or interesting tools!  Don't get
too fixated
on
absolute speed; the goal is to explore ideas, and that can absolutely be
done without breaking any performance records!
Is there a prize?
Besides eternal fame and glory?
If you submit an interesting write-up, I will buy you a coffee or drink
if we happen to be in the same city.  It will be particularly easy for
Cambridge / Boston / Somerville residents to receive their prize; I make no
guarantees for submissions from farther afield.
Background material
Interval Arithmetic and Recursive Subdivision for Implicit Functions and
Constructive Solid Geometry
(Duff '92) is a great introduction to common
techniques.  In particular, the combination of interval arithmetic, spatial
subdivision, and expression simplification remains the basis for modern
renderers.
These ideas are also presented in Â§3.7 of my thesis,
Hierarchical Volumetric Object Representations
for Digital Fabrication Workflows
(2013),
although my personal implementations have evolved since then (see below for
examples).
Finally, I gave a talk titled
Implicit Surfaces & Independent Research
(2025), which covers all of this material and hews closely to my
current implementations.  The audience was CS undergraduates in their senior
year, so it's intended to be approachable!
Gallery
Massively Parallel Rendering of Complex Closed-Form Implicit Surfaces
Matt Keeter, 2020
Paper homepage

bytecode, then executes it with a s

data.title: CO2 laser enables long-range detection of radioactive material
data.author: EA-3167
data.article_summary: 研究团队使用短脉冲CO₂激光器在10米距离外成功探测到放射性物质，这一距离是此前方法的十倍多。传统探测器如盖革计数器只能在接近放射源的情况下工作，而新方法通过探测放射性物质使空气电离产生的自由电子和负离子，利用CO₂激光引发电子雪崩效应，产生微等离子体并散射激光，从而实现远距离探测。实验中使用了3.6毫居里的钋-210作为α粒子源，并通过测量背散射光信号和等离子体荧光，确认放射源的存在和类型。尽管CMOS相机需靠近源进行成像，但该技术有望应用于核灾难响应和核安全领域，未来可能扩展至超过100米的探测距离。

43441082.article_content:
Detectors and sensors
Detectors and sensors
Research update
CO
2
laser enables long-range detection of radioactive material
19 Mar 2025
Remote detection
The ability to locate radioactive material at distances greater than the range of emitted particles could play an important role in nuclear disaster response and nuclear security. (Courtesy: Shutterstock/fewerton)
Researchers have demonstrated that they can remotely detect radioactive material from 10 m away using short-pulse CO
2
lasers – a distance over ten times farther than achieved via previous methods.
Conventional radiation detectors, such as Geiger counters, detect particles that are emitted by the radioactive material, typically limiting their operational range to the material’s direct vicinity. The new method, developed by a research team headed up at the
University of Maryland
, instead leverages the ionization in the surrounding air, enabling detection from much greater distances.
The study may one day lead to remote sensing technologies that could be used in nuclear disaster response and nuclear security.
Using atmospheric ionization
Radioactive materials emit particles – such as alpha, beta or gamma particles – that can ionize air molecules, creating free electrons and negative ions. These charged particles are typically present at very low concentrations, making them difficult to detect.
Senior author
Howard Milchberg
and colleagues – also from Brookhaven National Laboratory, Los Alamos National Laboratory and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory – demonstrated that CO
2
lasers could accelerate these charged particles, causing them to collide with neutral gas molecules, in turn creating further ionization. These additional free charges would then undergo the same laser-induced accelerations and collisions, leading to a cascade of charged particles.
This effect, known as “electron avalanche breakdown”, can create microplasmas that scatter laser light. By measuring the profile of the backscattered light, researchers can detect the presence of radioactive material.
The team tested their technique using a 3.6-mCi polonium-210 alpha particle source at a standoff distance of 10 m, significantly longer than previous experiments that used different types of lasers and electromagnetic radiation sources.
“The results are highly impressive,” comments
EunMi Choi
from the Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology in South Korea. Choi’s team had used a
gyrotron source to detect radioactive materials
back in 2017.
“The researchers successfully demonstrated 10-m standoff detection of radioactive material, significantly surpassing the previous range of approximately 1 m,” she says.
Milchberg and collaborators had previously used a
mid-infrared laser in a similar experiment
in 2019. Changing to a long-wavelength (9.2 μm) CO
2
laser brought significant advantages, he says.
“You can’t use any laser to do this cascading breakdown process,” Milchberg explains. The CO
2
laser’s wavelength was able to enhance the avalanche process, while being low energy enough to not create its own ionization sources. “CO
2
is sort of the limit for long wavelengths on powerful lasers and it turns out CO
2
lasers are very, very efficient as well,” he says. “So this is like a sweet spot.”
Imaging microplasmas
The team also used a CMOS camera to capture visible-light emissions from the microplasmas. Milchberg says that this fluorescence around radioactive sources resembled balls of plasma, indicating the localized regions where electron avalanche breakdowns had occurred.
By counting these “plasma balls” and calibrating them against the backscattered laser signal, the researchers could link fluorescence intensity to the density of ionization in the air, and use that to determine the type of radiation source.
The CMOS imagers, however, had to be placed close to the measured radiation source, reducing their applicability to remote sensing. “Although fluorescence imaging is not practical for field deployment due to the need for close-range cameras, it provides a valuable calibration tool,” Milchberg says.
Scaling to longer distances
The researchers believe their method can be extended to standoff distances exceeding 100 m. The primary limitation is the laser’s focusing geometry, which would affect the regions in which it could trigger an avalanche breakdown. A longer focal length would require a larger laser aperture but could enable kilometre-scale detection.
Choi points out, however, that deploying a CO
2
laser may be difficult in real-world applications. “A CO₂ laser is a bulky system, making it challenging to deploy in a portable manner in the field,” she says, adding that mounting the laser for long-range detection may be a solution.

data.title: 600M years of shared environmental stress response found in algae and plants
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 研究团队通过生物信息学方法比较了藻类和植物在6亿年间独立进化出的环境压力反应，发现它们共享一个应激反应网络。这项由哥廷根大学领导的研究发表在《Nature Communications》上。研究重点关注了与陆地植物关系最密切的接合藻类（zygnematophytes），通过高通量测序和应激条件下基因与代谢产物的分析，揭示了藻类和苔藓在数小时内的反应。研究发现，尽管这些生物在进化上已分离6亿年，但它们共享一些关键的基因“枢纽”，这些枢纽在应激反应网络中起重要作用。该研究为探索植物多样性中的生理影响提供了综合数据集。

• PaulHoule具体推荐了一本书，表明他对该书在计算机科学与生物学之间的侧重有明确偏好。这可能对那些同样对生物信息学中的计算方面更感兴趣的人有帮助。

• hsshhshshjk的问题引发了一个关于学习路径的讨论，潜在的讨论方向包括不同类型的学习资源（如书籍、在线课程）的优缺点，以及哪些资源适合初学者。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明显的争议，但不同的学习偏好可能导致对推荐资源的不同看法。例如，有些人可能更喜欢PaulHoule推荐的重计算机科学的书籍，而另一些人可能更倾向于寻找生物学和计算机科学平衡的资源。

PaulHoule推荐了一本偏重计算机科学的书籍，而hsshhshshjk则在寻找入门生物信息学的建议。讨论的核心在于如何选择适合自己兴趣和背景的学习资源。

The GIST
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies

Editors

the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
peer-reviewed publication

proofread
600 million years of shared environmental stress response found in algae and plants
by
University of Göttingen
The star-shaped algae Zygnema circumcarinatum shows similar stress reactions to the moss (microscope image). Credit: Tatyana Darienko
Without plants on land, humans could not live on Earth. From mosses to ferns to grasses to trees, plants are our food, fodder and timber. All this diversity emerged from an algal ancestor that conquered land long ago. The success of land plants is surprising because it is a challenging habitat. On land, rapid shifts in environmental conditions lead to stress, and plants have developed an elaborate molecular machinery for sensing and responding.
Now, a research team led by the University of Göttingen has compared algae and plants that span 600 million years of independent evolution and pinpointed a shared stress response
network
using advanced bioinformatic methods. The results were
published
in
Nature Communications
.
The closest algal relatives of land plants are the filamentous and unicellular conjugating algae, the zygnematophytes. This group of organisms has received major attention because when researchers compared data about land plants with data about these algae, they could trace back to the very first plants on land. One of the big questions is how the earliest
land plants
overcame terrestrial stressors.
To find out, the team generated hundreds of samples from a moss model system and two zygnematophyte algae challenged by environmental stressors found on land. Using high-throughput sequencing of the active genes and profiling of the compounds produced by the moss and
algae
under stress, they obtained a comprehensive picture of how the organisms react to the challenges over a course of several hours. By combining evolutionary analysis with statistical modeling and machine learning methods, a shared network of gene regulation was predicted.
The branching moss Physcomitrium patens, which the researchers used to study stress reactions and compare them to algae (microscope image). Credit: Tatyana Darienko
Professor Jan de Vries of Göttingen University, who led the research, explains, "One of the big surprises was that we found several highly connected genes—known as 'hubs'—in the network shared by these very different organisms that actually split from each other in evolutionary terms around 600 million years ago. These hubs appear to bundle information and shape the overall network response."
"Now we have a comprehensive dataset of stress responses, combining genetic and biochemical information that can be further explored for its physiological impact across plant diversity," adds Dr. Tim Rieseberg, first author of the study and also at Göttingen University.

data.title: Lua, a Misunderstood Language
data.author: soapdog
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了对Lua语言的误解，特别是针对一些人抱怨Lua缺乏“内置电池”（即标准库功能不足）的问题。作者认为，Lua本质上是一种提供机制而非策略的工具包，开发者可以根据需求自由扩展和定制，而不是让语言本身提供过多预设功能。Lua的设计初衷是嵌入到其他应用程序中作为脚本语言使用，其核心优势在于灵活性和可嵌入性，而非作为独立的全功能语言。作者还回应了关于Lua数组采用1基索引的批评，指出这种设计更符合人类习惯，而非像C语言那样基于内存偏移量的0基索引。总体而言，Lua的力量在于其简洁和灵活，只有将其嵌入到其他语言编写的软件中使用时，才能真正体会其独特之处。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lua编程语言的优缺点及其适用场景

不同观点：
• **norir**：认为Lua在代码量小于10k行的情况下表现出色，尤其在启动延迟和执行速度上有明显优势，能够提供接近即时的反馈，非常适合快速迭代开发。然而，随着项目规模扩大，缺乏类型系统和某些语法问题成为障碍。为了解决这些问题，norir选择使用Lua编写编译器来创建新语言，最终不再使用Lua。

• **bigfishrunning**：对Lua的基于1的索引（1-based indexing）提出批评，认为这不符合精确计算的要求，引用Dijkstra的观点支持其立场，认为人类思维本质上是不精确的。

• **Lasher**：分享了在Aardwolf MUD游戏中使用Lua替代"mobprog"脚本的成功经验，认为Lua非常适合作为嵌入式脚本语言来扩展游戏功能，但在构建完整应用程序时可能不是理想选择。

• **vitiral**：支持Lua的强大功能，提到正在使用Lua编写整个技术栈，认为Lua是非常出色的开发语言。

• **gowld**：指出Lua的开放性，特别提到Lua团队或LuaRocks团队不会像Elm社区那样干预开发者的工作，避免了不必要的社区争端。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Lua的1-based indexing是一个争议点，部分开发者如bigfishrunning对此持批评态度，认为不符合精确计算的需求。
• **适用场景**：Lua在小型项目和嵌入式脚本场景（如游戏扩展）中表现出色，但随着项目规模和复杂性增加，缺乏类型系统和某些语法问题成为限制因素。
• **扩展与定制**：norir通过Lua创建新语言来解决其遇到的问题，展示了Lua的灵活性和可扩展性。
• **社区与生态**：gowld提到Lua社区的开放性与Elm社区的对比，强调了Lua社区的自由和无干扰特点。

43463376.article_content:
Lua, a misunderstood language
Lua
is one of my favourite programming languages. I’ve used it to build a CMS for my old educational website, for creating cool IoT hardware projects, for building little games, and experimenting with network decentralisation. Still, I don’t consider myself an expert on it at all, I am at most a somewhat competent user. This is to say that I have had exposure to it in various contexts and through many years but I am not deep into its implementation or ecosystem. Because of that, it kinda pains me when I read blog posts and articles about Lua that appear to completely miss the objective and context of the language. Usually these posts read like a rant or a list of demands. Most recently, I saw a post
about Lua’s Lack of Batteries on LWN
and a
discussion about that post on Hacker News
that made me want to write back. In this post I’ll address some of the comments I’ve seen on that original article and on Hacker News.
Lua should be considered a toolkit
I think it was Hisham who in
his talk in LuaConf 2017
said that Lua is minimalistic (aka:
“there are zero ways to do it”
). This was of course about Lua offering mechanisms over policies, or how it unlocks agency in the developer by letting them adapt the language to suit their environment and not vice versa. Lua should be viewed as a base ingredient to which you add whatever you want. If you are making fruit smoothies, Lua is the milk and you add whatever fruits you need.
People who want batteries want a ready-made powertool full of opinions. They are not looking towards Lua in the context that Lua wants to exist. It is like looking at a boat and complaining it can’t fly. It was not meant to fly. Unless you build the rest of the place and make an hydroplane out of it. It is up to you, Lua doesn’t care.
Lua has always been a language for scripting applications. It has always been assumed that you’d build your domain specific code using something else and embed a Lua engine in it to make it flexible. Are you building games? You build your whole engine in whichever language makes sense for you game, including the domain specific stuff that only your game cares about, and then add Lua to it so that you can script and tweak your game without recompiling the source.
The same context applies to other software that offers Lua as the scripting language for their plugins or add-ons, this is what Lua has been built for, it offers advantages to this approach. The fact that you can write the whole software in Lua is a side-effect of it being a good language but it was not the primary use-case for it.
People who wants battery-included Lua do not realise that there are plenty of battery-included Lua distributions floating in the wild. Other developers picked Lua, added what they thought was a good baseline, and are shipping a complete package. You too can build your own battery-included Lua that has the stuff you want. We don’t need blessing from the Lua team at PUC to do it. This is how it is supposed to work. You pick the language and assemble what you need.
This leads to robust software since the developer are responsible for making the calls. You are in complete control and can make the decisions that are suitable for your development. There is no situation where Lua team, or LuaRocks team, can prevent you from doing what you want like the drama that has been happening inside the Elm community. You can grab the source for the version you want, and then never again look at Lua community.
I think that you can only appreciate Lua when you embed it on your own software. Until what you are building is a combination of some code in other language (such as C) and Lua, the power of Lua will not click for you. Not only the power, but
the way of Lua
will not click for you. If all you’re using is 100% Lua source code, it will feel just like another scripting languageânot unlike Python, or Rubyâand you will start trying to analyse Lua in terms of those other languages, which are not really comparable since they have different objectives.
Complaints about 1-based indexing for arrays
Mentioned in
this comment.
I often see this kind of complain from people who think that the C way of doing things is the only valid way. It would be great if people spent more time thinking about why use a 0-based index instead. C uses such indexes because the value is actually a multiplier that you can use to find the memory offset for the location of the data. If you have an array, and thus a pointer to the starting position for that data in memory, and you know the size of the array elements, you can multiply the size by the index, sum with the pointer value, and get the data that corresponds to the element referenced by that index. That is it. Indexes are zero based to help you find stuff in memory when you have a pointer which is basically all that C gives you.
Using 1 as the initial position for an array makes sense when you’re talking like a human. When you and your

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成教学材料工具的潜力和问题

不同观点：
• [支持并看好工具的发展前景]
  - [devgoncalo] 认为该工具具有视觉上的关键差异化优势，可能引领一种新的学习方式，并对工具的未来表示期待。
  - [teruakohatu] 表示该工具在高等教育领域有潜力，尤其是在开发入门课程时可以作为一个起点。
  - [julienmarie] 认为该工具可用于员工培训，尤其是在需要深度知识的情况下，尽管发现幻灯片中存在重复概念。

• [对AI生成内容质量的质疑]
  - [DanHulton] 强调AI生成的幻灯片往往质量平庸，无法与精心制作的演示文稿相比。认为AI工具可能在加剧教师工作负担问题，而不是解决根本问题。
  - [cube00] 分享了使用该工具的负面体验，指出AI生成的内容冗长且无助于学习目标的实现，同时还存在错误和图像版权问题。

• [对工具改进的建议]
  - [pratikshelar871] 建议使用更好的图像模型来将文本转化为插图，并提出通过构建现有LMS的集成来降低用户采纳门槛。
  - [gus_massa] 对幻灯片的文本过多和样式问题提出了改进建议，并询问了技术细节和使用成本。

• [对教师工作负担和资源共享的讨论]
  - [pbhjpbhj] 建议将教师优化后的幻灯片上传回系统，供其他教师使用，并提出通过版税激励来吸引和留住用户。
  - [_puk] 提到教师在材料制作上花费了大量时间，AI工具在这一领域有潜力显著改善教师的生活质量。

补充讨论：
• [技术问题]
  - [ako] 报告了在iPad上的使用问题，无法越过弹出对话框。

• [与其他工具的比较]
  - [fanssex] 提到类似工具https://pageon.ai/，并提醒注意该工具背后的公司背景。

• [创意整合]
  - [TKAU] 建议整合python库manim和ChatGPT，以创建数学动画，增强数学概念的可视化。

• [个人合作兴趣]
  - [topbenteacher] 表示对该工具有兴趣，并提到自己正在开发的AI辅助学习网站，表达了未来合作的意愿。

争议焦点：
• AI生成内容的质量与教师工作负担之间的矛盾，以及技术工具是否在解决或加剧这一问题。

data.title: Gatehouse – a composable, async-friendly authorization policy framework in Rust
data.author: hardbyte
data.article_summary: Gatehouse是一个灵活的授权库，结合了基于角色的访问控制（RBAC）、基于属性的访问控制（ABAC）和基于关系的访问控制（ReBAC）策略。其主要特性包括：支持多范式授权、策略组合（通过逻辑运算符AND、OR、NOT）、详细的评估跟踪、流式构建器API、类型安全以及异步支持。核心组件包括策略 trait、PermissionChecker（用于聚合多个策略）和 PolicyBuilder（用于构建自定义策略）。库中还包含内置策略如 RbacPolicy、AbacPolicy 和 RebacPolicy，以及策略组合器如 AndPolicy、OrPolicy 和 NotPolicy。示例代码展示了如何使用这些功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust应用中的权限策略引擎实现及其相关设计和工具问题

不同观点：
• jzelinskie：认为该项目提供了一种轻量级的方式在Rust应用中实现策略，并赞赏了其构建器的易用性。同时指出，单靠策略引擎不足以完成授权，还需要数据支持，且数据不一定总是在请求上下文中。他希望策略引擎能为如何获取数据提供更好的开发体验（DX），而不是像OPA生态那样事后填补空白。

Gatehouse
A flexible authorization library that combines role-based (RBAC), attribute-based (ABAC), and relationship-based (ReBAC) access control policies.

43466221.article_summary: Gatehouse是一个灵活的授权库，结合了基于角色的访问控制（RBAC）、基于属性的访问控制（ABAC）和基于关系的访问控制（ReBAC）策略。其主要特性包括：支持多范式授权、策略组合（通过逻辑运算符AND、OR、NOT）、详细的评估跟踪、流式构建器API、类型安全以及异步支持。核心组件包括策略 trait、PermissionChecker（用于聚合多个策略）和 PolicyBuilder（用于构建自定义策略）。库中还包含内置策略如 RbacPolicy、AbacPolicy 和 RebacPolicy，以及策略组合器如 AndPolicy、OrPolicy 和 NotPolicy。示例代码展示了如何使用这些功能。

data.article_summary: 2024年1月至2月间，德国联邦议院进行了多次重要投票，涉及多个领域的政策。1月17日，关于向乌克兰提供TAURUS巡航导弹的提案被否决，反对票占73%。1月18日，旨在支持和减轻农业负担的提案也被否决，反对票占62%。同日，AfD党提出的乌克兰与俄罗斯和平倡议获得89%的支持。1月19日，国籍法现代化提案通过，60%的议员支持。2月1日，联邦选举法修改提案通过，57%的议员支持。2月22日，关于加强对乌克兰支持的提案以57%的支持率通过，而CDU/CSU提出的德国外交与安全政策调整提案被否决。同日，促进经济增长的法案通过，58%的议员支持。2月23日，大麻管理法获得64%的支持，而欧盟海军部队ASPIDES的提案也通过。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用Git和GitHub管理法律文本的实践及其潜在价值和局限性

不同观点：
• [支持观点] nikeee提到德国议会使用GitHub存储法律文本，并通过Pull Request（PR）进行法律修改，这使得法律修改历史清晰可见，有助于提高透明度。maxekman支持这种做法，并表示考虑在瑞典政府API中采用类似项目以增强透明度。slt2021进一步强调这种做法有助于实时跟踪法律修改过程，特别是在美国预算和立法过程中，防止暗箱操作。zoobab甚至提出未来可以让公民直接提交法律改进建议。

• [质疑实用性] codedokode认为仅将法律文本添加到GitHub中并不足够，因为缺乏商业法律数据库中的常见功能，如交叉引用和相关案例链接。他还指出，GitHub可能仅能作为存储文档的工具，而不能用于解决实际法律问题。

• [技术细节讨论] lucb1e和ThinkBeat指出评论中的"git contributions graph"更准确地应为"GitHub contribution graph"。yallpendantools质疑该项目中"Git"的独特性，认为其与GitHub的贡献日历类似。YmiYugy则希望看到更多版本控制系统（VCS）功能应用于法律文本管理，如git blame和git log。

• [政治与技术结合] agnishom和qrush对德国议会使用GitHub管理法律投票的实践进行了调侃，qrush更是幽默地称议会“晋升为经理”。

• [系统局限性与改进] rwoerz指出某些投票结果可能会产生误导，因为它们涉及决策建议和原始请求的否定关系。n2d4感叹大多数政府数据难以访问，希望有更多像这样优秀的政府数据聚合器。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还涉及到Git和GitHub的区别，sam_lowry_提醒不要将两者混淆，并批评GitHub属于美国垄断企业。
• 对法律文本管理和透明度的技术实现存在不同看法，部分评论强调现有系统的局限性，而另一些评论则看好其未来的发展潜力。

By
Greg Kamradt
Published 24 Mar 2025
ARC-AGI-2 + ARC Prize 2025 is Back
Level Up to Reach AGI
Good AGI benchmarks act as useful progress indicators. Better AGI benchmarks clearly discern capabilities. The best AGI benchmarks do all this and actively inspire research and guide innovation.
At ARC Prize, our mission is to serve as a North Star towards AGI through enduring benchmarks, directing efforts towards systems capable of general intelligence and significantly compressing the timeline for scientific breakthroughs.
ARC-AGI-1 has measured progress towards AGI since 2019 and was the only benchmark to
pinpoint the exact moment in late 2024
when AI moved beyond pure memorization. OpenAI used ARC-AGI-1 to demonstrate this progress with their o3 system which combines deep learning-based LLMs with reasoning synthesis engines.
ARC Prize 2024 inspired thousands of independent
students
and
researchers
to work alongside frontier labs on new test-time adaption ideas.
But there is more work to do to reach AGI. AGI still needs new ideas.
We can characterize systems like o3 as going from "zero to one" on the fluid intelligence spectrum. But these systems are highly inefficient and currently require significant human supervision during the training process to adapt to new domains.
Announcements
Today we’re excited to launch ARC-AGI-2 to challenge the new frontier. ARC-AGI-2 is even harder for AI (in particular, AI reasoning systems), while maintaining the same relative ease for humans. Pure LLMs score 0% on ARC-AGI-2, and public AI reasoning systems achieve only single-digit percentage scores. In contrast, every task in ARC-AGI-2 has been solved by at least 2 humans in under 2 attempts.
Alongside it, today we're announcing
ARC Prize 2025
(going live on Kaggle this week), designed to drive open-source progress on highly efficient, general systems capable of beating ARC-AGI-2.
Easy for Humans, Hard for AI
All other AI benchmarks focus on superhuman capabilities or specialized knowledge by testing "PhD++" skills. ARC-AGI is the only benchmark that takes the opposite design choice – by focusing on tasks that are relatively easy for humans, yet hard, or impossible, for AI, we shine a spotlight on capability gaps that do not spontaneously emerge from "scaling up".
The ARC Prize Foundation adapts this into our definition for measuring AGI: the gap between the set of tasks that are easy for humans and hard for AI. When this gap is zero, when there are no remaining tasks, we can find that challenge AI, we will have achieved AGI.
Addressing these capability gaps requires novel insight and new ideas. Importantly, ARC-AGI does not exist purely to measure AGI progress. It also exists to inspire researchers to work on new ideas.
Intelligence requires the ability to generalize from limited experience and apply knowledge in new, unexpected situations. AI systems are already superhuman in many specific domains (e.g., playing Go and image recognition.) However, these are narrow, specialized capabilities. The "human-ai gap" reveals what's missing for general intelligence - highly efficiently acquiring new skills.
Introducing ARC-AGI-2
The ARC-AGI-2 benchmark launches today. This second edition in the ARC-AGI series raises the bar for difficulty for AI while maintaining the same relative ease for humans.
Every ARC-AGI-2 task was solved by at least 2 humans in 2 attempts or less in a controlled study with hundreds of human participants. This matches the rules we hold for AI, which gets two attempts per task.
ARC-AGI-1, introduced in 2019, was designed to challenge deep learning. Specifically, it was designed to resist the ability to simply "memorize" the training dataset. ARC-AGI comprises a training dataset and several evaluation sets, including a private eval set used for the ARC Prize 2024 contest. The training set is intended to teach the Core Knowledge Priors required to solve tasks in the evaluation sets. To solve the evaluation tasks, AI systems must demonstrate basic fluid intelligence or the ability to adapt to novel, never-before-seen tasks.
As an analogy, think of the training set as a way to learn grade school math symbols, and the evaluation set requires you to solve algebra equations using your knowledge of those symbols. You cannot simply memorize your way to the answer, you must apply existing knowledge to new problems.
Any AI system capable of beating ARC-AGI-1 demonstrates a binary level of fluid intelligence. In contrast, ARC-AGI-2 significantly raises the bar for AI. To beat it, you must demonstrate
both
a high level of adaptability and high efficiency.
While designing ARC-AGI-2, we studied these properties of frontier AI reasoning systems. Below are example tasks to illustrate some of what we discovered. All of the following tasks are part of ARC-AGI-2 and were (1) solved by at least 2 humans in under 2 attempts and (2) unsolved by any frontier AI reasoning system.

data.title: Intel: A Bug and a Pro
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了1994年英特尔公司在其Pentium处理器中发现的一个浮点除法错误（FDIV Bug）以及P6处理器的发布。尽管英特尔在个人电脑微处理器市场占据了约75%的份额，并成功进入了其他多个领域，但Pentium处理器在处理某些浮点除法运算时出现了计算错误。1994年6月，林奇堡学院的教授Thomas R. Nicely在研究双素数倒数时发现该问题，并于10月确认是硬件错误。他通过邮件告知英特尔，但英特尔仅表示问题已知，未提供详细信息。Nicely进一步验证发现，Pentium处理器在计算如1/824633702441等数值时返回错误结果。尽管该错误只影响极少数用户，但因英特尔初期处理不当，最终导致召回和更换问题芯片，损害了公司声誉。与此同时，Pentium处理器在性价比上表现优异，与RISC CPU竞争有力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Intel处理器历史上的FDIV bug、市场策略以及硬件错误检测功能的讨论。

不同观点：
• [rwmj]: 提到Linux使用Coe's ratio（4195835/3145727）来检测FDIV bug，并提供了相关代码和文献链接。这表明了操作系统如何应对历史上的硬件缺陷问题。

• [jeffs4271]: 对MIPs R8000在2025年被提及感到惊讶，认为该CPU较为 obscure，尽管它针对HPC但整数工作负载表现较弱。分享了个人参与相关项目的经历，并认为该项目很有趣。

• [jmclnx]: 提到F00F bug，并指出IBM停止出货有缺陷的PC迫使Intel解决问题。同时质疑现代IBM是否会采取类似行动。

• [bendercorn]: 补充提到Intel市场和公关部门推出的用户测试计划，以确保高级用户能提前获得PPro系统来检测潜在的FDIV问题。指出Nicely和作曲家John Williams是首批接受者。

• [ankitg12]: 提供了一个相关讨论的链接，指向之前在Hacker News上的讨论。

• [adrian_b]: 批评Intel的市场决策，尤其是将CPU产品线分为Pentium和Pentium Pro，并取消了消费级CPU的内存错误检测功能以刺激专业用户购买更昂贵的Pro版本。认为这导致了广泛的经济损失和潜在的数据损坏问题，并质疑Intel声称取消该功能是为了降低计算机价格的说法。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Intel在1990年代中期对CPU产品线的市场分割策略，尤其是取消消费级CPU的内存错误检测功能，这被认为对消费者不利。
• 另一个讨论点是历史上硬件缺陷（如FDIV bug）对行业的影响以及操作系统如何通过软件手段进行应对。
• 对不同CPU（如MIPs R8000和Intel Pentium/Pro）的历史表现和市场定位的个人评价和回忆。

By 1994, Intel had managed to capture about 75% of the microprocessor market for personal computers. The company had also found its way into automobiles, industrial controls, telecommunications equipment, and supercomputers. The Intel x86 architecture had propelled the company to these immense heights, and they’d established a cadence of releases in that CPU line of roughly four years. The investment that both individuals and companies had made in hardware and software for the architecture was measured in billions.
While the Pentium had been announced on the 22nd of March in 1993, systems built around the Pentium were announced on the 17th of May in 1993, and volume shipments didn’t occur until later in the year. The Pentium’s 60MHz variant could deliver 100 million instructions per second with the Dhrystone 1.1 benchmark while the 66MHz variant bumped that to 112MIPS. These were the first x86 chips to be capable of this kind of performance, and they nearly doubled the performance of the original i486. This kind of performance nearly put Intel in competition with RISC-based UNIX workstation hardware, and Intel’s biggest software partner, Microsoft, supported those workstations with
NT
. A key difference, however, was that the Pentium’s price was around $900 while the MIPS R8000 was around $2500 and the Alpha 21064 was over $3000. Naturally, these were all far more reasonably priced when purchased in volume, but Intel was far better in terms of performance per dollar. For less than the cost of a high performance RISC CPU, a customer could purchase an entire Pentium-based PC that, while not as powerful, was capable of the same kinds of work. This is remarkable as PC manufacturers were running into the problems already solved by workstation makers: thermals, volatage variation, RFI, EMI. These kinds of considerations hadn’t been too big a hill to climb with an XT, but they were far more serious issues with a Pentium. They were serious enough that Intel had provided thermal models to system makers before they had provided the silicon.
Early in 1994, Intel announced the Pentium P54C for Socket 5. These chips required a 3.3 volt power supply, could run at 75MHz, 90MHz, or 100MHz, and utilized an internal clock multiplier allowing them to operate at a higher frequency than the external buses. These chips bumped the transistor count to 3.3 million, and were built on a half micron BiCMOS process. These Pentiums also added support for use in multiprocessor systems which was the primary source of the increased transistor count. When adding a processor, a machine needs more circuitry for cache, memory, interrupts, and bus utilization.
While most news for Intel was great, not all of it was. A few of the first generation Pentium processors were in the hands of Professor Thomas R. Nicely at Lynchburg College in Virginia where they were put to work researching reciprocals of twin prime numbers. On the 13th of June in 1994, Nicely noted that after adding three Pentium-based computers to his lab, he was getting inconsistent results in floating point divisions. He ruled out all causes other than hardware error on the 19th of October. Specifically, Nicely noted that 1 divided by 824633702441 was incorrect on three different Pentium systems while it was correct on multiple i486 and i386 systems. He then sent an email to Intel on the 24th documenting his discovery. Intel didn’t provide much information to him beyond stating that the issue was known. He then sent an email to several other people on the 30th. His email read:
It appears that there is a bug in the floating point unit (numeric coprocessor) of many, and perhaps all, Pentium processors.
In short, the Pentium FPU is returning erroneous values for certain division operations. For example, 1/824633702441.0 is calculated incorrectly (all digits beyond the eighth significant digit are in error). This can be verified in compiled code, an ordinary spreadsheet such as Quattro Pro or Excel, or even the Windows calculator (use the scientific mode), by computing (824633702441.0)*(1/824633702441.0), which should equal 1 exactly (within some extremely small rounding error; in general, coprocessor results should contain 19 significant decimal digits). However, the Pentiums tested return 0.999999996274709702 for this calculation. A similar erroneous value is obtained for x*(1/x) for most values of x in the interval 824633702418 <= x <= 824633702449, and throughout any interval obtained by multiplying or dividing the above interval by an integer power of 2 (there are yet other intervals which also produce division errors).
