The Great Barefoot Running Hysteria of 2010
03/25/25 • 9 minute read
The year was 2010.  “Ke$ha's Tik Tok”  was topping the Billboard charts.  Steve Jobs has just introduced a goofy new oversized iPhone called an “iPad”.  And in running forums across the internet far and wide, hoards of enthusiasts preached the gospel of a new way of running: without shoes.
Google Trends interest in "Barefoot Running" from 2004 to present
The “Great Barefoot Running Hysteria of 2010”, as I call it, took the amateur running world by storm.  Propelled by dramatic claims of performance improvements and injury prevention, barefoot running gave rise to a vocal (and often militant) contingent of enthusiasts and entirely new classes of footwear.  And then over the course of a several years, it faded away almost as quickly as it came, leaving behind changes in running shoes and culture forever.  In this post, we'll explore the history and legacy of the barefoot running movement.
The Barefoot Running Movement & How It Started
Barefoot running is–of course–as old as humanity itself. In fact, people have run barefoot throughout most of human history, with the practice continuing today in several cultures, such as Kenya and indigenous peoples in Mexico.
In this sense, before addressing the modern origins of
barefoot
running, we need to talk about the origins of
shod
running
.
The concept of running shoes as we understand them today, specifically designed to improve running efficiency and comfort, did not emerge until the late 19th and early 20th centuries. This evolution coincided with the rise of organized sports and recreational running, which spurred the development of footwear tailored to the specific needs of runners.
The first breakthrough came in 1865 when an English shoemaker brilliantly suggested adding spikes to otherwise normal-looking dress shoes to make them suitable for cross-country running. Later, in the early 20th century, shoes with rubber soles were introduced, offering improved grip and shock absorption, marking a significant advancement in the design of running shoes.
The result of these running shoe trends was running shoe stores filled with bulky, over-engineered clown shoes that promised to prevent running injuries, but probably didn't.
Into more modern times, running shoes continued to evolve past their humble beginnings into heavier, more complex footwear with exotic materials like plastics & EVA foam.  In the 80s and 90s, many shoemakers became fixated on
stability
and the notion that pronation, the natural roll of the foot after it lands, was a cause for running injuries.  Running shoes were increasingly designed to try to prevent this movement with wedges of foam that support and stabilize the arch of the foot, a high heel-to-toe drop, and other questionable features like plastic air bubbles in the heel to cushion the foot with each step.
The result of these running shoe trends was running shoe stores filled with bulky, over-engineered clown shoes that promised to prevent running injuries, but probably didn't, and were mostly just uncomfortable to use. You can see an example of this kind of design in action in the Nike Air Max 90, which is now also available in a more tasteful re-issue.  While the original was marketed as a running shoe, the modern re-issue is a nostalgic fashion shoe that you should definitely
not
run in.
The original Nike Air Max 90
A modern re-issue of the Nike Air Max 90 (from
Nike.com
)
The barefoot running renaissance can thus be understood as a backlash to the dominant running shoe trends at the time.  The revival was driven by a growing dissatisfaction with traditional running shoes, which many believed contributed to injuries and impeded natural foot movement. Proponents of barefoot running argued that it encouraged a more natural gait, reducing the impact on the legs and back and enhancing the overall running experience.
In 2004, inspired by Stanford athletes training barefoot, Nike introduced the
Nike Free
, a running shoe that bucked the bulky running shoe trends of the time with a super flexible sole and a minimal heel-to-toe offset.
The original Nike Free (via Wikipedia)
Then, in 2006, Vibram launched the 5-Fingers: a shoe intended to be as close to barefoot as possible, with a thin rubber sole and glove-like fit for the toes.  This was the shoe that truly ushered in the
minimalist
mindset: running shoes should enable a "natural" gait and that
less is more
.
Vibram 5 Fingers (via Amazon)
The barefoot-inspired
Nike Free
and
Vibram 5 Fingers
set the stage, but the real barefoot running revolution began not with a pair of shoes, but with a book about an indigenous tribe of Native Mexicans.
Christopher McDougall's "Born to Run"
While the over-engineered running shoe backlash had already started with shoes like the Nike Free and the Vibram 5 Fingers, the spark that lit the barefoot running powder keg was Christopher McD

data.title: Btrfs Adding Fast/Realtime ZSTD Compression and Other Performance Optimizations
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Linux 6.15内核中Btrfs文件系统的更新，主要包括性能优化和新功能。Btrfs将支持更快的新Zstd压缩级别（-1到-15），通过牺牲压缩比提升速度，并增加了对负压缩级别的支持和defrag ioctl处理。此外，若文件需要校验和，Btrfs现在可回退到缓冲写入以避免校验和不匹配错误。其他改进包括发送路径的优化（提升约30%的运行时性能）、稳定写入支持、folio API转换及子页面清理等。整体上，Btrfs在Linux 6.15中将获得多项性能和功能增强。

43468842.article_content:
Btrfs Adding Fast/Realtime Zstd Compression & Other Performance Optimizations
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Linux Storage
on 24 March 2025 at 02:29 PM EDT.
9 Comments
David Sterba of SUSE sent in all of the Btrfs file-system updates today for the now-open
Linux 6.15
kernel merge window. There are some new performance optimizations, new and faster Zstd compression level options, and other changes slated to be included for this CoW file-system in Linux 6.15.
Btrfs for Linux 6.15 has prepared fast/real-time Zstd compression levels from -1 to -15 for the transparent file-system compression support. With a mount option like "compress=zstd:-5" the negative compression levels can be set for improving speed albeit reducing the compression ratio.
Daniel Vacek of SUSE added the negative Zstd compression levels support for Btrfs and provided some numbers on that patch series:
The Btrfs defrag ioctl has also been extended to handle the negative compression levels for Zstd.
The Btrfs code for Linux 6.15 is now also able to fallback to using buffered writes if direct I/O is attempted on a file that requires checksums. This fallback to using buffered writes will avoid checksum mismatch errors albeit with slower performance than direct IO.
Btrfs for the next kernel version also now considers its sub-page mode to be "reasonably complete and tested" and thus no longer warning users over its use.
Some of the other performance work for Btrfs in Linux 6.15 includes enhancing the send path so there is better file path caching that can yield around a 30% run-time improvement on a sample workload. There is also a minor speed improvement within the encoded read code path.
Btrfs is also enabling stable writes on inodes, more folio API conversions, sub-page clean-ups, and a variety of other improvements and fixes.
More details on these proposed Btrfs changes for Linux 6.15 via
this pull request
.

data.title: Vertical farming company Plenty files for bankruptcy after raising nearly $1B
data.author: iancmceachern
data.article_summary: 垂直农业公司Plenty宣布破产，并在声明中表示已获得2,070万美元的债务人持有融资以支持重组计划。公司计划继续运营位于弗吉尼亚的草莓农场和怀俄明的植物科学研发中心。自2014年成立以来，Plenty已筹集近10亿美元资金，投资方包括SoftBank、沃尔玛、Bezos Expeditions等。近年来，垂直农业行业屡受打击，Bowery Farming、AeroFarms和AppHarvest等公司也面临财务困境或破产。

43468876.article_content:
Vertical farming company
Plenty
has
filed for bankruptcy
, the company said in a press release on Monday.
In its statement,
Plenty
said it has received a commitment for $20.7 million in debtor-in-possession financing as part of a proposed restructuring plan. It plans to continue to operate a strawberry farm in Virginia and a plant science research and development (R&D) center in Wyoming.
Debtor-in-possession financing is financing for firms in Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
Since its 2014 inception, South San Francisco-based Plenty has raised nearly $1 billion in funding from a variety of investors, including SoftBank Investment Advisers, Walmart, Bezos Expeditions, and Jeff Bezos as an angel investor.
Its last known valuation was $1.9 billion at the time of
a $400 million Series E fundraise
in January 2022, according to PitchBook.
The industry has been hard hit by bankruptcies in recent years. In November 2024, agtech unicorn Bowery Farming was reported to be
shutting down
after raising more than $700 million in funding and last being valued at $2 billion in 2021. And in 2023, AeroFarms and AppHarvest filed for bankruptcy protection. AeroFarms had raised more than $300 million from backers before filing for bankruptcy. In September 2023, it
exited bankruptcy protection
fully funded.
AppHarvest
raised more than $700 million before being taken public in 2021 at a $1 billion valuation; it filed for Chapter 11 protection in 2023.

data.author: jimminyx
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了音质如何在数字交流中影响他人对我们的印象。耶鲁大学心理学家Brian Scholl发现，在视频会议中，音质差会导致听众对讲话者的智力、可信度和吸引力产生负面评价，即使内容相同。通过一系列实验，研究者证实，刺耳的声音会让听众认为讲话者不那么适合雇佣或约会。这表明，人们在潜意识中会根据声音质量做出判断，而不是仅仅依赖于话语内容。因此，改善麦克风质量可以提升他人对你的印象，特别是在面试或约会等场合。这项研究强调了在数字交流中关注音质的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：麦克风选择和使用的复杂性，以及音频录制的准备和培训

不同观点：
• 观点一：麦克风的选择取决于环境和部署情况。ggm 提到自己使用过非常昂贵和便宜的麦克风，发现哪种更好是条件性的。他个人推荐 Røde Lavalier 领夹麦克风，认为其性价比高且具有全向拾音的特点。

• 观点二：方向性强的麦克风虽然音质好，但在实际使用中可能不方便，例如在视频会议中会显得突兀。ggm 提到自己曾使用过 USB-C 的播客麦克风，虽然音质好但体积大，不方便使用。

• 观点三：音频录制中环境噪音的控制是一个挑战，尤其是在使用全向麦克风时。ggm 认为完全隔绝外界噪音并非总是理想，适量的环境音可以增加真实感。

• 观点四：专业培训对提高录音质量非常重要。ggm 提到公司曾资助他参加澳大利亚影视学校的课程，由一位经验丰富的电台专业人士授课，这对他提高录音技巧有很大帮助。

补充讨论：
• 关于“即兴录制”：ggm 强调即兴录制实际上99%靠规划，在电台工作中几乎不存在真正的即兴录制，尽可能提前做好准备是关键。

• 争议焦点：在选择麦克风时，价格和性能之间的关系并不是绝对的。ggm 的经验表明，便宜的麦克风在特定条件下也能提供出色的表现，因此不一定要追求最贵的设备。

总结来看，评论主要围绕麦克风选择、使用环境、噪音控制和录音培训的重要性展开，强调实际情况中需要综合考虑多种因素，并且做好充分准备。

To Win Trust and Admiration, Fix Your Microphone
From job interviews to dating, we subconsciously judge one another based on sound quality when we interact digitally
By
Rachel Nuwer
edited by
Sarah Lewin Frasier
yasinemir/Getty Images
Like hundreds of millions of others around the world, Brian Scholl, a psychologist and cognitive scientist at Yale University,
spent much of the COVID pandemic on Zoom
. But during one digital faculty meeting, he found himself reacting unexpectedly to two colleagues. One was a close collaborator with whom Scholl usually saw eye-to-eye, while the other was someone he tended to have differing opinions from. On that particular day, though, he found himself siding with the latter colleague. “Everything he said was so rich and resonant,” Scholl recalls.
As he reflected afterwards, Scholl realized that there was a key underlying difference between the two men’s messaging: the colleague whom Scholl normally agreed with had been using a junky built-in microphone on an old laptop, whereas the one with whom he typically disagreed had called in from a professional-grade home-recording studio. Scholl began to suspect that it was the quality of their sound, rather than the content of their arguments, that had swayed his judgment.
New research
published in the
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
suggests his hunch was correct. In a series of experiments, Scholl and his colleagues found that poor audio quality consistently caused listeners to negatively judge speakers in a variety of contexts—even if the message itself was exactly the same.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by
subscribing
. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
“When chatting on Zoom, everyone is familiar with how they look, but we don’t typically take into account how we sound to other people,” Scholl says. “It turns out this can really drive people’s impressions of how intelligent you are, how credible you are and how datable and hirable you are.”
Our brain evolved to make intuitive judgments about people not solely on the basis of what they say but also according to how they sound. Ample research has shown that factors such as
how confident
a person sounds or whether
they have an accent
influence how others perceive them. Scholl wanted to see if the same pattern would hold when the only difference was technological distortion.
Scholl, Robert Walter-Terrill and Joan Danielle Ongchoco, both then graduate students at Yale, created audio recordings in which a human man or woman or a computerized male or female voice read one of three scripts. Each script dealt with a different topic: the readers posed as a job applicant, a potential romantic partner and someone describing a car accident. Some of the recordings were clear, whereas others were artificially manipulated to sound tinny. “We tried to use a manipulation that’s relevant to daily life,” Scholl says. “If you spend time on Zoom, you probably know tons of people who sound like this.”
The researchers recruited more than 5,100 people online and had each participant listen to one script and then answer simple questions about their judgment of the speaker on a continuous scale. The team ensured that the participants actually understood what they had heard by asking some of them to transcribe the recording they heard after they answered the questions.
Across all three scripts, and for both human and computerized voices, participants consistently rated the tinny voices as less hirable, datable, credible and intelligent. The findings speak to the “deep power of perception,” Scholl says, and its ability to make us behave irrationally. “Everybody knows that this kind of auditory manipulation does not reflect on the person themselves,” he says. “But our perception is operating, in some ways,
autonomously from higher-level thought
.”
Nadine Lavan, a psychologist at Queen Mary University of London, who was not involved in the research, says the findings are somewhat expected based on what researchers already knew about how we evaluate other people. “But a lack of surprise doesn’t mean the results are not important or interesting,” she says.
The study raises questions, she continues, about how much of an effect microphone quality may or may not have in real-world settings. Job applicants, for example “don’t tend to read out their applications; they tend to give more spontaneous answers,” Lavan says. “Also, abstract ratings of credibility and of being hirable are informative, but real-life hiring decisions tend to include higher stakes and much more complex trading off of different factors.”
Assuming the findings do hold in the real world to some extent, Scholl says the takeaway lesson is clear: “You should really find out how you sound to other people online.

data.title: What is Growth Engineering? A deep dive with MasterClass's former Head of Growth
data.author: stosssik
data.article_summary:
《什么是增长工程？》由Gergely Orosz和Alexey Komissarouk撰写，深入探讨了增长工程领域，该领域介于产品工程和市场营销之间。十年前，增长工程鲜为人知，但现在许多科技公司都有专门的增长团队。

**主要内容包括：**
1. **定义**：增长工程是通过编写代码帮助公司赚更多钱，重点在于优化客户旅程，如吸引新用户、转化付费客户、提高用户留存和消费。
2. **工作内容**：包括面向业务的工作、赋能和平台建设。
3. **速度**：增长工程师比产品工程师行动更快，因为他们以“学习为目的”进行开发，常采取一些短期有效的捷径。
4. **技术栈**：涉及常见编程语言、监控、功能标志和实验、产品分析等。
5. **适合的人**：具有好奇心、“学习为目的”心态以及“多面手”特质的人。
6. **职业发展**：适合想成为创始人或产品经理的人，能加速职业发展，并深入了解业务。

Alexey分享了自己的经历，通过一个推送通知实验为公司创造了每年150万美元的额外收入，展示了增长工程的实际效果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于工程师是否应接受适当的统计学和实验设计培训，以避免在数据分析中出现错误。

不同观点：
• Naijaboiler认为工程师在进行数据分析时需要接受适当的统计学和实验设计培训。他指出，在没有事先设计实验和明确测量指标的情况下，事后通过SQL查询数据并挑选有利统计结果的做法是不严谨的，容易导致错误结论。他强调这种事后分析方法通常不如精心设计的实验可靠，并建议工程师如果想扮演分析师或数据科学家的角色，应该去学习相关统计知识。

• 另一种观点可能来自那些支持灵活数据分析的从业者，他们认为即使没有事先设计的实验，通过探索性数据分析和事后验证，仍然可以获得有价值的见解。这种观点强调了数据分析的实践性和适应性，尤其是在快速变化的技术环境中。

补充讨论：
• Naijaboiler提到准实验技术（quasi-experimental techniques）可以在某种程度上帮助推断因果关系，但通常不如精心设计的实验可靠。这表明在数据分析中存在多种方法，每种方法都有其优缺点。

• 评论中还隐含了对跨领域工作的批评，特别是工程师在不具备足够统计知识的情况下进行数据分析工作。这涉及到对多技能角色（如增长工程师）的专业性要求和职业边界问题的讨论。

争议焦点：主要争议在于工程师是否应具备足够的统计知识来进行有效的数据分析，以及事后分析的有效性和可靠性问题。Naijaboiler显然对此持批评态度，强调专业培训和实验设计的重要性。

Before we start: if you’ve already filled out the
What is your tech stack? survey
: thank you! If you’ve not done so, your help will be greatly appreciated. It takes 5-15 minutes to complete. Those filling out will receive results before anyone else, and additional analysis from myself and Elin.
Fill out this survey here.
Fill out the survey
Growth engineering was barely known a decade ago, but today, most scaleups and many publicly traded tech companies have dedicated growth teams staffed by growth engineers. However, some software engineers are still suspicious of this new area because of its reputation for hacky code with little to no code coverage.
For this reason and others, I thought it would be interesting to learn more from an expert who can tell us all about the practicalities of this controversial domain. So I turned to
Alexey Komissarouk
, who’s been in growth engineering since 2016, and was in charge of it at online education platform, MasterClass. These days, Alexey lives in Tokyo, Japan, where he
advises on growth engineering
and teaches the
Growth Engineering course
at
Reforge
.
In today’s deep dive, Alexey covers:
What is Growth Engineering?
In the simplest terms: writing code to help a company make more money. But there are details to consider: like the company size where it makes sense to have a
dedicated
team do this.
What do Growth Engineers work on?
Business-facing work, empowerment and platform work are the main areas.
Why Growth Engineers move faster than Product Engineers
. Product Engineers ship to build: Growth Engineers ship to learn. Growth Engineers do take shortcuts that would make no sense when building for longevity – doing this on purpose.
Tech stack.
Common programming languages, monitoring and oncall, feature flags and experimentation, product analytics, review apps, and more.
What makes a good Growth Engineer?
Curiosity, “build to learn” mindset and a “Jack of all trades” approach.
Where do Growth Engineers fit in?
Usually part of the engineering department, either operating as with an “owner” or a “hitchiker” model.
Becoming a Growth Engineer.
A great area if you want to eventually become a founder or product manager – but even if not, it can accelerate your career growth. Working in Growth forces you to learn more about the business.
With that, it’s over to Alexey:
I’ll never forget the first time I made my employer a million dollars.
I was running a push notification A/B test for meal delivery startup
Sprig
, trying to boost repeat orders.
A push notification similar to what we tested to boost repeat orders
Initial results were unpromising; the push notification was not receiving many opens. Still, I wanted to be thorough: before concluding the idea was a failure, I wrote a SQL query to compare order volume for subsequent weeks between customers in test vs control.
The SQL used to figure out the push notification’s efficiency
As it turned out, our test group “beat” the control group by around 10%:
‘review_5_push’ was the new type of push notification. Roughly the same amount of users clicked it, but they placed 10% more in orders
I plugged the numbers into a
significance calculator
, which showed it was statistically significant – or “stat-sig” – and therefore highly unlikely to be a coincidence. This meant we had a winner on our hands! But how meaningful was it, really, and what would adding the push notification mean for revenue, if rolled out to 100% of users?
It turned out this experiment created an additional $1.5 million dollars, annually,
with just one push notification.
Wow!
I was hooked. Since that day, I've shipped hundreds of experimental “winners” which generated hundreds of millions of incremental revenue for my employers. But you never forget the first one. Moments like this is what growth engineering is all about.
1. What
is
Growth Engineering?
Essentially, growth engineering is the writing of code to make a company money. Of course, all code produced by a business on some level serves this purpose, but while Product Engineers focus on creating a Product worth paying for, Growth Engineers instead focus on making that good product have a good business. To this end, they focus on optimizing and refining key parts of the customer journey, such as:
Getting more people to consider the product
Converting them into paying customers
Keeping them as customers for longer, and spending more

data.title: My Favorite C++ Pattern: X Macros (2023)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了C++中一种称为“X宏”的模式，该模式主要用于代码生成，特别适合处理大量重复代码的情况，如声明多个变量或类、执行相似操作等。作者以Chapel编译器中的字符串驻留（String Interning）为例，展示了如何使用X宏来简化和自动化代码编写。通过在一个头文件中定义宏列表，开发者可以在多个地方“迭代”该列表以生成所需的代码，从而减少手动编写和维护重复代码的工作量。文章还提到该模式在抽象语法树（AST）类层次结构中的应用，展示了其广泛的实用性。使用X宏不仅提高了代码的可维护性，还减少了添加新代码时的出错风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X-Macros 的使用及其在 C 和 C++ 中的适用性

不同观点：
• Kragen 认为 X-Macros 更偏向于 C 语言的模式，而不是 C++。他分享了自己使用 X-Macros 处理 VNC 协议消息类型的经验，并提供了具体实现示例，展示了如何通过宏自动生成序列化与反序列化代码。
• Jchw 认为 X-Macros 虽然是经典的 C++ 模式，但其流行度不如其他技术。他指出，如果 C++ 的宏更强大，许多 X-Macros 的使用场景可以被单一宏替代。他还提到了一种通过 bin2c 转换生成字节数组文本的技巧。
• Loeg 表示虽然不喜欢 X-Macros，但承认其在某些情况下非常有用，例如生成错误码枚举和字符串表。
• Blackthorn 更倾向于使用外部代码生成脚本，而不是依赖预处理器宏。
• Malkia 提到在 LuaJIT 源码中见过类似的宏使用方式，并分享了自己在封装 C API 时的经验。
• Wat10000 建议通过更具描述性的宏名称和一些预处理器技巧来改进 X-Macros 的使用。
• Kevin_thibedeau 认为通过将宏作为参数传递可以避免在同一翻译单元中使用多个宏的问题。
• Gibibit 认为 X-Macros 在 C 中可能比在 C++ 中更有用，但需要注意不要过度使用。
• PaulHoule 提到 X-Macros 在 IBM 360 汇编语言中的历史应用，指出其在数据模式构建中的作用。
• RandomNumber7 认为使用这些技巧解决实际问题是有用的，但质疑是否存在更简单的语言可以替代。
• Sfpotter 认为使用 D 语言可以避免这些问题。
• KerrAvon 强烈反对使用 X-Macros，认为这种预处理器与代码混合的方式难以调试和维护，是一种反模式。
• A_t48 认为 X-Macros 有用，但更希望用其他方式替代。
• Lowbloodsugar 用“fruit lists”来称呼这类技巧。

补充讨论：
• X-Macros 的优缺点：支持者认为它在特定场景下非常有用，如代码生成和表维护；反对者则认为它难以维护，容易导致技术债务。
• 历史背景：X-Macros 并非新技巧，其历史可追溯到 1960 年代，并在不同语言和环境中都有应用。
• 替代方案：一些评论者提到使用外部脚本生成代码或采用其他编程语言（如 D 语言）作为替代方案。

争议焦点：X-Macros 是否应在现代 C++ 开发中广泛使用，特别是在其可维护性和复杂性方面存在较大分歧。

My Favorite C++ Pattern: X Macros
C++
Chapel
Compilers
Posted on October 14, 2023.
Table of Contents
When I first joined the
Chapel
team,
one pattern used in its C++-based compiler made a strong impression on me. Since
then, Iâve used the pattern many more times, and have been very satisfied with
how it turned out. However, it feels like the pattern is relatively unknown, so
I thought Iâd show it off, and some of its applications in the
Chapel compiler
. Iâve slightly tweaked
a lot of the snippets I directly show in this article for the sake of simpler
presentation; Iâve included links to the original code (available on GitHub)
if you want to see the unabridged version.
Broadly speaking, the âX Macrosâ pattern is about generating code. If you have a
lot
of repetitive code to write (declaring many variables or classes, performing
many very similar actions, etc.), this pattern can save a lot of time, lead
to much more maintainable code, and reduce the effort required to add
more
code.
I will introduce the pattern in its simplest form with my first example:
interning strings
.
Application 1: String Interning
The Chapel compiler interns a lot of its strings. This way, it can reduce the
memory footprint of keeping identifiers in memory (every string
"x"
is
actually the
same
string) and make for much faster equality comparisons
(you can just perform a pointer comparison!). Generally, a
Context
class
is used to manage interning state. A new interned string can be constructed
using the context object in the following manner:
UniqueString
::
get
(
ctxPtr
,
"the string"
);
Effectively, this performs a search of the currently existing unique strings.
If one with the content (
"the string"
in this case) doesnât exist, itâs
created and registered with the
Context
. Otherwise, the existing string is
returned. Some strings, however, occur a lot in the compiler, to the point that
it would be inefficient to perform the whole âfind-or-createâ operation every
time. One example is the
"this"
string, which is an identifier with a lot of
special behavior in the language (much like
this
in languages such as Java).
To support such frequent flier strings, the compiler initializes them once,
and creates a variable per-string that can be accessed to get that stringâs value.
Thereâs that repetitive code. Defining a brand new variable for each string,
of which there are around 100 at the time of writing, is a lot of boilerplate.
There are also at least two places where code needs to be added:
once in the declaration of the variables, once in the code that initializes them.
[note:
A third use in the compiler is actually a variadic template defined over
character arrays. The template is defined and specialized in such a way that
you can refer to a variable by its string contents (i.e., you can write
USTR("the string")
instead of
theStringVariable
).
]
It would be very easy to accidentally modify the former but not the latter,
especially for developers not familiar with how these âcommon stringsâ are
implemented.
This is where the X Macros come in. If you look around the compiler source code,
thereâs a header file that looks something like the following:
From
all-global-strings.h
, around line 31
X
(
align
,
"align"
)
X
(
atomic
,
"atomic"
)
X
(
bool_
,
"bool"
)
X
(
borrow
,
"borrow"
)
X
(
borrowed
,
"borrowed"
)
X
(
by
,
"by"
)
X
(
bytes
,
"bytes"
)
// A lot more of these...
Whatâs this
X
thing? That right there is the essence of the pattern: the macro
X
isnât defined in the header!
Effectively,
all-global-strings.h
is just
a list, and we can âiterateâ over this list to generate some code for each
one of its elements, in as many places as we want. What I mean by this is
that we can then write code like the following:
From
global-strings.h
, around line 76
struct
GlobalStrings
{
#define X(field, str) UniqueString field;
#include
"all-global-strings.h"
#undef X
};
In this case, we define the macro
X
to ignore the value of the string (weâre
just declaring it here), and create a new
UniqueString
variable declaration.
Since the declaration is inside the
GlobalStrings
struct, this ends up
creating a field. Just like that, weâve declared a class with over 100
fields. Initialization is equally simple:
From
Context.cpp
, around line 49
GlobalStrings
globalStrings
;
Context
rootContext
;
static
void
initGlobalStrings
()
{
#define X(field, str) globalStrings.field = UniqueString::get(&rootContext, str);
#include
"chpl/framework/all-global-strings.h"
#undef X
}
With this, weâve completely automated the code for for both declaring and
initializing all 100 of our unique strings. Adding a new string doesnât require
a developer to know all of the places where this is implemented: just by
modifying the
all-global-strings.h
header with a new call to
X
, they can
add both a new variable and code to initialize it. Pretty robust!

data.title: Hann: A Fast Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search Library for Go
data.author: habedi0
data.article_summary: Hann 是一个用于 Go 语言的高性能近似最近邻搜索库，支持在高维空间中进行高效的相似性搜索。它提供了多种索引数据结构，包括 HNSW（层次导航小世界图）、PQIVF（乘积量化倒排文件）和 RPT（随机投影树）。Hann 具有统一的索引接口，支持任意维度向量的索引和搜索，并利用 SIMD（AVX）指令加速距离计算。它还支持批量插入、删除、更新向量，以及将索引保存到磁盘和加载。Hann 适用于构建向量数据库或为 Go 应用添加快速的内存相似性搜索功能。安装需 Go 1.21 及以上版本、C/C++ 编译器和支持 AVX 指令的 CPU。

• [oldgregg] 对该库表示赞赏，但更关注如何用Go语言原生方式从文本生成向量，表明他关心功能扩展及Go语言生态中的实现方式。

Hann
A fast approximate nearest neighbor search library for Go
Hann is a high-performance approximate nearest neighbor search (ANN) library for Go.
It provides a collection of index data structures for efficient similarity search in high-dimensional spaces.
Currently, supported indexes include Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW),
Product Quantization Inverted File (PQIVF), and Random Projection Tree (RPT).
Hann can be seen as a core component of a vector database (like Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, etc.).
It can be used to add fast in-memory similarity search capabilities to your Go applications.
Features
Unified interface for different indexes (see
core/index.go
)
Support for indexing and searching vectors of arbitrary dimension
Fast distance computation using SIMD (AVX) instructions (see
core/simd_distance.c
)
Support for bulk insertion, deletion, and update of vectors
Support for saving indexes to disk and loading them back

Supported Distances
The HNSW index supports the use of Euclidean, squared Euclidean, Manhattan, and cosine distances.
If cosine distance is used, the vectors are normalized on read (before they are used in the index or for search).
Note that squared Euclidean distance is slightly faster to compute than Euclidean distance
and gives the same order of closest vectors as Euclidean distance.
It can be used in place of Euclidean distance if only the order of closest vectors to
query vector is needed, not the actual distances.
The PQIVF and RPT indexes support Euclidean distance only.

43470162.article_summary: Hann 是一个用于 Go 语言的高性能近似最近邻搜索库，支持在高维空间中进行高效的相似性搜索。它提供了多种索引数据结构，包括 HNSW（层次导航小世界图）、PQIVF（乘积量化倒排文件）和 RPT（随机投影树）。Hann 具有统一的索引接口，支持任意维度向量的索引和搜索，并利用 SIMD（AVX）指令加速距离计算。它还支持批量插入、删除、更新向量，以及将索引保存到磁盘和加载。Hann 适用于构建向量数据库或为 Go 应用添加快速的内存相似性搜索功能。安装需 Go 1.21 及以上版本、C/C++ 编译器和支持 AVX 指令的 CPU。

data.title: Polypane, The browser for ambitious web developers
data.author: ulrischa
data.article_summary: Polypane是一款强大的网站开发和测试工具，帮助开发者在不切换上下文的情况下，全面处理网站的响应式设计、可访问性、元数据和性能等问题。它支持在同一界面查看从手机到5K显示器的各种视口，提供实时结构、元数据和无障碍检查建议。开发者可以并排查看深色和浅色模式，而无需更改系统设置。所有操作如点击、滚动、输入和样式编辑等都能在多设备间同步。该工具速度快，功能强大，深受前端开发者好评，能够发现和解决不同断点间的间距问题，并提供出色的调试工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Polypane浏览器的功能、定价模式、必要性以及与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• 支持与赞赏：
  - Polypane用户（如imjackofitall、runekaagaard、jamesmkenny）表示该浏览器帮助他们提高了工作效率，尤其是响应式设计和会话管理功能。他们还赞赏了其出色的客户支持（例如Kilian在Slack上快速解决问题）。
  - 用户（runekaagaard）特别指出Polypane能够很好地模拟设备问题，而Chrome无法做到这一点。

• 质疑与比较：
  - 用户（culi、machine_ghost）质疑Polypane是否真的需要作为一个独立浏览器存在，认为Firefox开发工具或Chrome已经提供了类似功能。
  - 用户（Ataraxic）关注Polypane在不同浏览器引擎（如Safari或Mozilla）中的局限性，并提到其基于Chromium可能无法完全模拟非Chromium浏览器的问题。

• 功能与定价建议：
  - 用户（bluetidepro、sureglymop、sam_goody）对订阅模式表示担忧，希望能有一次性购买选项或学生折扣。sam_goody提出了一种折中方案，即支付一段时间的费用后继续使用但不更新。
  - 用户（cantSpellSober）询问Polypane相对于BrowserStack的功能优势，以及是否集成GenAI工具，以便向经理推销。

• 免费与替代方案：
  - 用户（tonijn）询问是否有免费替代品，而short_sells_poo则表示支持付费产品，认为免费产品通常通过数据挖掘和广告盈利。

补充讨论：
- Polypane开发者Kilian亲自回应，表示愿意回答任何问题，显示了开发者与用户之间的互动。
- 一些用户（如masto）表示在了解Polypane之前已经通过其他工具解决了类似问题，但认为Polypane本可以节省他们的时间。
- 争议焦点在于Polypane的定价模式和其相对于现有免费工具的附加价值。

data.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: VGGT（Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer）是一个由牛津大学和Meta AI合作开发的前馈神经网络，能够在数秒内从一张或多张图像中推断出场景的关键3D属性，包括相机参数、深度图、3D点图和3D点轨迹等。该模型易于安装和使用，通过克隆代码库并安装依赖项即可运行。VGGT支持自动下载预训练权重，并可在Hugging Face上手动获取。用户可以根据需要选择预测不同的属性，如相机参数、深度图和点图，并通过提供的函数将深度图转换为3D点图，或跟踪特定点的3D轨迹。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于VGGT模型及其在3D重建中的应用和潜力的讨论

不同观点：
• [正面评价] [w-m] 对论文持积极态度，赞赏作者的成果和呈现方式，尤其是模型在不同注意力机制和归一化方法上的处理。尽管肯定了模型的表现，但也提到该研究缺乏“顿悟”时刻，更多依赖大数据和大量计算资源，呼应了《苦涩的教训》一文中的观点。
• [应用建议] [sgnelson] 希望将此技术与传统摄影测量学结合，作为手机3D扫描的补充工具，而不是完全取代传统方法。
• [质疑] [bhouston] 对论文中户外示例的可靠性提出质疑，认为这些示例可能因为训练集中包含相关数据而存在偏差，尤其是著名地标如金字塔和罗马斗兽场。
• [实用性疑问] [davedx] 对该技术的实际应用场景感到困惑，特别是商业应用方面的具体用例不明确。
• [技术对比] [porphyra] 指出该研究与先前方法（如COLMAP、NERF、Gaussian Splatting）的对比，强调了使用Transformer可以从更少图像中重建场景的优势。
• [实验反馈] [jdthedisciple] 对模型在Huggingface上的表现提出批评，认为点云结果遗漏了输入图像中一半的特征，表现一般。
• [技术扩展] [vessenes] 关注模型在密集点云和splats上的应用潜力，建议通过微调或重新训练来提升模型在该领域的表现。
• [功能需求] [richard___] 强调需要在动态场景中使用相机姿态的技术。
• [术语批评] [amelius] 对使用电气工程领域的术语表示不满。
• [应用设想] [maelito] 询问该技术是否可用于构建类似Google Earth的3D场景。
• [AGI展望] [ninetyninenine] 认为AGI将是多种模型拼接而成，VGGT模型可能成为感知领域的一部分。
• [娱乐性评论] [fallingmeat] 以幽默方式要求看到视频演示，否则难以相信结果。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于模型的创新性和实用性。部分评论者如[w-m]和[bhouston]对模型的创新性持保留态度，认为更多依赖大数据和计算资源，而非新颖的算法设计。而[porphyra]则肯定了模型在减少图像需求方面的进步。
• 实际应用场景是另一个讨论重点。评论者如[sgnelson]和[davedx]对技术如何落地提出了疑问和建议，特别是对手机3D扫描和商业应用的潜力进行了探讨。
• 技术细节方面，评论涉及了模型在不同任务（如splats和动态场景）上的扩展和优化潜力，以及对实验结果的具体反馈。

43470651.article_summary: VGGT（Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer）是一个由牛津大学和Meta AI合作开发的前馈神经网络，能够在数秒内从一张或多张图像中推断出场景的关键3D属性，包括相机参数、深度图、3D点图和3D点轨迹等。该模型易于安装和使用，通过克隆代码库并安装依赖项即可运行。VGGT支持自动下载预训练权重，并可在Hugging Face上手动获取。用户可以根据需要选择预测不同的属性，如相机参数、深度图和点图，并通过提供的函数将深度图转换为3D点图，或跟踪特定点的3D轨迹。

data.title: What Killed Innovation?
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了数据可视化领域的创新停滞问题。作者在2012年进入该领域，当时D3.js刚推出，互动图形蓬勃发展。然而，十年后，作者发现可视化项目变得千篇一律，缺乏新意。通过与业界专家的讨论，作者提出了几个原因：新闻编辑室数字化、JavaScript成熟以及D3.js的早期创新为网络实验奠定了基础，但近年来，互动网络项目趋于同质化，商业投资减少。作者指出两个主要变化：首先是“scrollies”（滚动叙述）的流行，虽然初期令人兴奋，但很快成为默认格式；其次，商业项目更倾向于使用模板化解决方案，导致创新减少。专家们认为需要反思和改变以重振该领域的创造力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据可视化的创新与实用性

不同观点：
• **支持传统实用性观点**：[janalsncm] 认为，数据可视化的核心目的是让人们容易理解数据，不断改变可视化方法只会让事情更复杂。例如，条形图在某些情况下是最优选择。创新应以实用性为基础，而非为了创新而创新。
• **创新间歇性出现观点**：[0xbadcafebee] 提出，创新往往以爆发形式出现，并在人类需求减少或开发难度增加时停滞。虽然对网络和网络应用平台持批评态度，但对未来的创新仍抱有希望，认为原生应用有更大的潜力。
• **数据素养与可视化欺骗性观点**：[praptak] 强调，复杂的可视化可能误导观众，尤其是当观众数据素养不高时。例如，饼图和颜色选择可能扭曲数据呈现。因此，对复杂可视化持怀疑态度是有道理的。
• **创新与一致性的平衡观点**：[Ragnarork] 认为，虽然寻找新的数据呈现方式是有价值的，但应以实用为前提，而非一味追求创新。过度创新可能增加消费者的理解负担。
• **具体案例批评观点**：[ralferoo] 通过具体案例（"512 paths to the white house"图形）指出，某些复杂可视化可能比实用更具迷惑性。传统的简单、清晰呈现方式可能更有效。

补充讨论：
• **创新经济性与价值观点**：[arscan] 和 [fullshark] 提到，高质量的可视化创新成本高且难以从中获取经济价值，导致该领域的创新减少。此外，某些创新形式（如2016年美国选举针图形）让人们对整个 genre 产生反感。
• **技术发展与标准化观点**：[jeffreyrogers] 认为，随着技术的发展，人们逐渐找到了解决数据可视化问题的标准方法，导致创新减少。例如，小提琴图（violin plot）是少数因统计学进步而产生的创新。
• **受众与呈现形式限制观点**：[WaitWaitWha] 提到，在实际工作中，由于受众和格式限制（如PowerPoint和PDF），即使团队内部使用创新的可视化解决方案，最终仍需回归传统形式。

争议焦点：
• 数据可视化创新的实用性与必要性之间的争议。一方认为创新能带来更好的数据理解方式，另一方则认为复杂创新可能增加理解难度，传统方法更为可靠。
• 可视化创新的经济性与受众接受度之间的矛盾。创新虽能带来一时的关注，但其经济价值和受众接受度限制了其广泛应用。

总结：讨论围绕数据可视化的创新与实用性展开，涵盖创新价值、受众需求、技术发展及经济性等多方面观点，并通过具体案例分析了复杂可视化的优缺点。

Mar 05, 2025
This is part of a trilogy on the state of our industry:
Part 1:
Outside a clientâs comfort zone
Part 2:
What killed innovation? A brief history
Part 3: (Coming soon)
I entered the data visualization field in 2012, when D3.js had just come out and interactive graphics were going through a digital Renaissance.  By the time I was fully steeped in the field in 2016, it felt like a new, experimental project was coming out every weekâeach one pushing the boundaries of how we think about, visualize, and communicate data.
New York Times'
512 Paths to the White House
from 2012.  When I think of the pre-scrollytelling era, it's always the first one I point to.
But fast forward a decade, and it feels like Iâm seeing the same polished but predictable formats over and over.
At first, I thought I had gotten jaded (a decade in tech feels like forever and maybe Iâm now just the old granny shaking my fist about the âgood old daysâ ð), but after talking to a few friends and mulling on it for a couple years, I now have some hypotheses on how we might have gotten here.
To test these hypotheses, I asked a few very respected voices in our industryâall known for their beautiful, bespoke work and responsible for driving the field forward in one way or another.  So Iâd like to thank everyone who kindly contributed: Nadieh Bremer, Giorgia Lupi, Federica Fragapane, Caitlin Ralph, Matt Daniels, RJ Andrews, Alberto Cairo, Eric William Lin, and Moritz Stefaner. While some of them are quoted directly, all of them provided insightful and nuanced answers that helped to shape my own whirlwind of ideas about where we are today, how we got here, and where weâre headed.
A brief history (of a plateau)
Let me come out swinging: our industryâs creativity has plateaued.
Ok, I donât fully mean that (but itâs got a lot of potential for a click-bait title, no? ð).  Let me provide a bit more nuance: the craft of telling data-informed stories on the web has plateaued.
As Alberto recounts, newsrooms started digitizing in the mid-to-late 1990s, and by the time I started in the early 2010s, the foundations were laid out for really interesting web-based experiments.  It was the perfect storm: Javascript was maturing, browser performance was improving, and D3.js was releasing interesting new layouts and supporting chart-specific interactions every year.  I was constantly coming across new chart forms, and new ways to add interactions and animations to layer information.  Just look at these two New York Times pieces from 2012 and 2013:
Four Ways to Slice Obamaâs 2013 Budget Proposal
(2012, left) and
Among the Oscar Contenders, a Host of Connections
(2013, right).  From a technical perspective, I remember being so mind-blown about how the different budget items animated so smoothly between the different views, and so inspired by the use of force-directed graph to lay out the Oscar nominees (and that visual elegance!).
It really seemed like no two data visualizations looked the same.
RJ agrees that web interactives âhit some kind of romantic peakâ in the mid-to-late 2010s.  Nadieh dreamily recalls the advent of D3 visuals like chord diagrams and circle packing. âI canât tell you what other mind boggling new technique or technology since then has, Iâve felt, made an impact,â she laments. âAnd that makes me very sad.â
Moritz summarizes his recent observations with the precision and insight of an industry veteran who has put out inspiration after inspiration for decades:
The few viral, well-known data visualizations tend to be static images or movies or small, personalized apps rather than elaborate interactive web pieces.
Visual styles are more homogenous,  with many projects looking similar due to the prevalence of established formats, templated solutions and software defaults.
On the commercial side, investments in bespoke data visualization from freelancers and independent studios have declined.
Moritz has written a whole blog post in response, with the most amazing title:
âWhy 2024 was a dead year for indie dataviz â and how weâll do much better in 2025â
.  Itâs well worth a thorough read.
He declares: âitâs a polycrisisâ.
But how did we get here (polycrisis)?
Over the past decade, Iâve noticed two fundamental shifts that have changed how we design interactive graphics on the web.
The first: scrollies.
I still remember when I first saw Stephanie Yee and Tony Chuâs
âA visual introduction to machine learningâ
in 2016, I was blown away:
It felt so exciting that web performance had come so far, that browsers could continuously scroll
and
animate thousands of elements at the same time. Scrollytelling was so quickly adopted that there was even a big debate about whether scrollies or steppers were âbetterâ (beautifully summarized
in this blog post
by Zan Armstrong). But the scrolly won out

data.title: Samsung CEO Jong-hee Han has died
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 三星首席执行官之一Jong-hee Han因心脏病去世，享年63岁。他于1988年加入三星，2011年成为产品研发负责人，后领导三星电视业务，2021年成为三星DX部门（合并移动和消费电子）负责人。2022年，他正式成为公司副董事长兼CEO。尽管他在领导DX部门前没有移动业务经验，但帮助三星连续15年占据全球电视销量榜首。Han最近主持了股东大会，就公司股票表现不佳道歉，并提到三星在人工智能半导体市场反应不足以及在半导体并购上面临监管问题，但承诺今年将取得实际成果。目前，他的联合首席执行官Young-Hyun Jun已成为公司唯一CEO。尚不清楚三星是否会任命新的CEO。

One of Samsung's CEOs, Jong-hee Han, has died due to a heart attack, according to
Reuters
and
CNBC
. He was 63. Han joined the company in 1988 and became the head of product research and development for visual display in 2011. He then led Samsung's TV business before he was named as the head of Samsung DX, which is what the company calls its
merged mobile and consumer electronics
divisions, in 2021. In 2022, he officially became the company's Vice Chairman and CEO. Han had no experience in mobile before he started leading the company's DX group, but Samsung gave him credit for helping it get to the top of global TV sales for 15 years.
CNBC
says Han was one of the executives who hosted Samsung's annual general shareholders meeting just a week ago and answered questions about the company's poor stock performance. During the meeting, Han
apologized
to the shareholders, telling them that Samsung "failed to adequately respond to the rapidly evolving AI semiconductor market." He also told the shareholders that Samsung was having difficulties when it came to semiconductor-related mergers and acquisitions due to regulatory issues, but that the company was "determined to produce some tangible results this year."
Based on the notice Samsung
published
, Han's co-CEO Young-Hyun Jun is now the sole CEO of the company. Jun, who also heads Samsung's semiconductor business, was appointed as Han's co-CEO in November 2024. It's not clear whether Samsung is planning to appoint another CEO in the future.

data.title: If you get the chance, always run more extra network fiber cabling
data.author: hggh
data.article_summary: 本文是博客作者Chris Siebenmann对使用过时浏览器访问其博客或wiki的用户的解释和提醒。由于2025年初高流量的爬虫（包括为LLM训练收集数据的爬虫）使用旧版浏览器用户代理，特别是Chrome的，作者采取了封锁措施。如果用户因误判而被挡，建议联系作者并提供浏览器的详细信息（如User-Agent字符串）。特别提到，使用archive.*（如archive.today, archive.ph）的用户可能因类似恶意爬虫的行为被挡，建议使用更规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络布线（尤其是光纤和以太网布线）的规划与实施，包括前期设计、预留空间、布线类型选择以及实际安装过程中遇到的问题和经验。

不同观点：
• [ggm] 和 [protocolture] 强调了在初期设计时需要考虑未来技术发展，比如光纤需求的增加，建议在设计时留出足够的冗余空间（plenum space）和布线容量。他们通过实际案例说明了前期不足可能导致的问题，比如Canary Wharf的plenum空间调整和电信大楼屋顶光纤核心不足的情况。
• [timzaman] 对上述观点持部分反对意见，认为在家庭或小型网络中过度布线是不切实际的，并且成本高昂。他建议在家庭布线中使用MTP/MPO等结构化电缆，并确保预留拉线（pullstring），以便将来可以轻松添加新电缆。
• [bhouston] 分享了自家布线的实际经验，强调了在设计阶段无法预见未来需求，导致布线不足的遗憾。他列举了多个后悔没有多布线的场景，如地下室、车库和天花板AP的布线不足。
• [JoshTriplett] 和 [jmacd] 强调了预埋管道（conduit）的重要性，以便将来可以轻松添加新电缆。他们通过实际经验说明了预埋管道在未来维护和扩展中的优势。
• [chaz6] 介绍了英国光纤宽带部署的立法环境和实际技术选择，如XGS PON和50G PON，并讨论了单点到多点（point-to-multipoint）技术在成本和扩展性上的优势。他还提到了不同ISP对光纤网络的支持情况和IPv6的实际应用问题。
• [aftbit] 和 [eqvinox] 讨论了单模（single mode）和多模（multi-mode）光纤的选择，认为在2025年及以后，单模光纤在各方面都更具优势，建议在新建项目中优先选择单模光纤。

补充讨论：
• [msarrel] 强调了布线过程中需要注意最小弯曲半径，并通过实际案例说明了在90年代因老鼠咬坏电缆导致的网络故障问题。
• [zelon88] 提出了随着无线技术（如WiFi）的发展，某些场景下对有线网络的需求有所减少，但仍需在初期设计中考虑足够的布线冗余。
• [js2] 和 [yetihehe] 通过幽默的方式指出了实际使用中可能遇到的意外情况，如动物进入机房导致的故障和因疫情导致家庭办公室位置变化的遗憾。

争议焦点：
• 布线时的前期投入与未来需求的平衡问题，即是否应该在初期投入更多以应对未来不确定的需求，还是通过预留管道和拉线等方式为将来扩展做准备。
• 单模光纤和多模光纤的选择，尤其是在2025年及以后的技术趋势中，哪种光纤类型更具优势。

43471177.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: Open-sourcing OpenPubkey SSH (OPKSSH): integrating single sign-on with SSH
data.author: PranaFlux
data.article_summary: OPKSSH（OpenPubkey SSH）是一个开源项目，旨在通过集成单点登录（SSO）技术（如OpenID Connect）简化SSH密钥管理，无需手动配置SSH密钥。它利用OpenPubkey协议将公钥添加到ID Tokens中，使其能够像证书一样使用，从而支持SSH协议的SSO认证，而无需更改现有的SSH或SSO协议。OPKSSH的优势包括提高安全性，通过使用短期有效的SSH密钥减少密钥泄露风险，并提升便利性，用户只需登录身份提供商（IdP）即可生成SSH密钥。该项目解决了传统SSH密钥管理中的安全和使用难题，特别适用于需要频繁访问和权限管理的企业环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过ID Tokens实现SSH认证的可行性及替代方案

不同观点：
• **zokier的观点**：认为ID Tokens不包含用户公钥，无法直接用于像SSH这样的安全协议。虽然SSH认证不一定要基于公钥，但这种方法缺乏直接性，错失了一个改进的机会。他建议可以通过GSSAPI或其他类似方法实现。
• **throw0101c的观点**：提出使用SSH证书的替代方案，通过建立内部SSH CA来实现短期证书认证，并提到一些自动化获取SSH证书的项目和商业产品。
• **_hyn3的观点**：比较了Userify的SSH密钥技术，认为其去中心化密钥和集中控制平面的方式更可靠，尤其是在认证服务器离线时。同时指出其依赖较多，增加了复杂性。
• **tptacek的观点**：赞赏这种证书认证方式，提到他们使用Teleport，具有类似的短 lived 证书认证功能，并强调其访问控制和审计日志的优势。
• **somat的观点**：希望看到如何通过SSH密钥登录网页，而非使用ID Tokens进行SSH认证。
• **password4321的观点**：提到一个支持X.509证书的OpenSSH分支，并提供相关技术文章链接。
• **bzmrgonz的观点**：关注该项目的安全性，质疑其代码构建的安全性，认为将认证过程转移到opkssh上需要进行安全审计。
• **samcat116的观点**：不确定这种方法与运行支持OIDC的SSH CA相比有何优势，认为服务器只需信任CA的密钥，而不必运行验证程序。
• **atonse的观点**：比较了这种方法与Tailscale SSH，并询问两者是否可能结合使用。
• **Aeolun的观点**：认为通过公钥返回标准和服务器端认证脚本来实现SSH登录并非新颖，自OpenID Connect发明以来就已可能实现。
• **kipz的观点**：对该技术表示赞赏，并愿意尝试。
• **znpy的观点**：指出通过AuthorizedKeysCommand等已有技术可以实现类似功能，认为这种方法并无太多新意，但对作者的实现表示肯定。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于这种新方法的实用性和创新性。部分用户认为它没有充分利用SSH协议的多认证方法特性，错失了改进机会；而另一部分用户则赞赏其创新和实用性。
• 安全性和代码审计也被多次提及，表明用户对新认证方法的安全性有较高关注。
• 多种替代方案（如SSH证书、Userify、Teleport、Tailscale SSH）被提出，展示了实现安全认证的多样性。

43470906.article_content:
Open-sourcing OpenPubkey SSH (OPKSSH): integrating single sign-on with SSH
2025-03-25
Ethan Heilman
7 min read
OPKSSH makes it easy to
SSH
with single sign-on technologies like OpenID Connect, thereby removing the need to manually manage and configure SSH keys. It does this without adding a trusted party other than your identity provider (IdP).
We are excited to announce
OPKSSH (OpenPubkey SSH)
has been open-sourced under the umbrella of the OpenPubkey project. While the underlying protocol
OpenPubkey
became
an open source Linux foundation project in 2023
, OPKSSH was closed source and owned by
BastionZero (now Cloudflare)
. Cloudflare has gifted this code to the OpenPubkey project, making it open source.
In this post, we describe what OPKSSH is, how it simplifies SSH management, and what OPKSSH being open source means for you.
Background
A cornerstone of modern access control is single sign-on
(SSO)
, where a user authenticates to an
identity provider (IdP)
, and in response the IdP issues the user a
token
. The user can present this token to prove their identity, such as âGoogle says I am Aliceâ. SSO is the rare security technology that both increases convenience â users only need to sign in once to get access to many different systems â and increases security.
OpenID Connect
OpenID Connect (OIDC)
is the main protocol used for SSO. As shown below, in OIDC the IdP, called an OpenID Provider (OP), issues the user an ID Token which contains identity claims about the user, such as âemail is
[email protected]
â. These claims are digitally signed by the OP, so anyone who receives the ID Token can check that it really was issued by the OP.
Unfortunately, while ID Tokens
do
include identity claims like name, organization, and email address, they
do not
include the userâs public key. This prevents them from being used to directly secure protocols like SSH or
End-to-End Encrypted messaging
.
Note that throughout this post we use the term OpenID Provider (OP) rather than IdP, as OP specifies the exact type of IdP we are using, i.e., an OpenID IdP. We use Google as an example OP, but OpenID Connect works with Google, Azure, Okta, etc.
Shows a user Alice signing in to Google using OpenID Connect and receiving an ID Token
OpenPubkey
OpenPubkey, shown below, adds public keys to ID Tokens. This enables ID Tokens to be used like certificates, e.g. âGoogle says
[email protected]
is using public key 0x123.â We call an ID token that contains a public key a
PK Token
. The beauty of OpenPubkey is that, unlike other approaches, OpenPubkey does not require any changes to existing SSO protocols and supports any OpenID Connect compliant OP.
Shows a user Alice signing in to Google using OpenID Connect/OpenPubkey and then producing a PK Token
While OpenPubkey enables ID Tokens to be used as certificates, OPKSSH extends this functionality so that these ID Tokens can be used as SSH keys in the SSH protocol. This adds SSO authentication to SSH without requiring changes to the SSH protocol.
Why this matters
OPKSSH frees users and administrators from the need to manage long-lived SSH keys, making SSH more secure and more convenient.
âIn many organizations â even very security-conscious organizations â there are many times more obsolete authorized keys than they have employees. Worse, authorized keys generally grant command-line shell access, which in itself is often considered privileged. We have found that in many organizations about 10% of the authorized keys grant root or administrator access. SSH keys never expire.â
Â
-
Challenges in Managing SSH Keys â and a Call for Solutions
by Tatu Ylonen (Inventor of SSH)
In SSH, users generate a long-lived SSH public key and SSH private key. To enable a user to access a server, the user or the administrator of that server configures that server to trust that userâs public key. Users must protect the file containing their SSH private key. If the user loses this file, they are locked out. If they copy their SSH private key to multiple computers or back up the key, they increase the risk that the key will be compromised. When a private key is compromised or a user no longer needs access, the user or administrator must remove that public key from any servers it currently trusts. All of these problems create headaches for users and administrators.
OPKSSH overcomes these issues:
Improved security:
OPKSSH replaces long-lived SSH keys with ephemeral SSH keys that are created on-demand by OPKSSH and expire when they are no longer needed. This reduces the risk a private key is compromised, and limits the time period where an attacker can use a compromised private key. By default, these OPKSSH public keys expire every 24 hours, but the expiration policy can be set in a configuration file.
Improved usability:
Creating an SSH key is as easy as signing in to an OP. This means that a user can SSH from any computer with opkssh installed, even if they havenât copied their SSH pri

• **tptacek的观点**：赞赏这种证书认证方式，提到他们使用Teleport，具有类似的短 lived 证书认证功能，并强调其访问控制和审计日志的优势。
• **somat的观点**：希望看到如何通过SSH密钥登录网页，而非使用ID Tokens进行SSH认证。
• **password4321的观点**：提到一个支持X.509证书的OpenSSH分支，并提供相关技术文章链接。
• **bzmrgonz的观点**：关注该项目的安全性，质疑其代码构建的安全性，认为将认证过程转移到opkssh上需要进行安全审计。
• **samcat116的观点**：不确定这种方法与运行支持OIDC的SSH CA相比有何优势，认为服务器只需信任CA的密钥，而不必运行验证程序。
• **atonse的观点**：比较了这种方法与Tailscale SSH，并询问两者是否可能结合使用。
• **Aeolun的观点**：认为通过公钥返回标准和服务器端认证脚本来实现SSH登录并非新颖，自OpenID Connect发明以来就已可能实现。
• **kipz的观点**：对该技术表示赞赏，并愿意尝试。
• **znpy的观点**：指出通过AuthorizedKeysCommand等已有技术可以实现类似功能，认为这种方法并无太多新意，但对作者的实现表示肯定。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于这种新方法的实用性和创新性。部分用户认为它没有充分利用SSH协议的多认证方法特性，错失了改进机会；而另一部分用户则赞赏其创新和实用性。
• 安全性和代码审计也被多次提及，表明用户对新认证方法的安全性有较高关注。
• 多种替代方案（如SSH证书、Userify、Teleport、Tailscale SSH）被提出，展示了实现安全认证的多样性。

data.title: The Hartlib Papers
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 《哈特利布文件》项目源于17世纪学者萨缪尔·哈特利布的愿景，他致力于记录人类所有知识并普及于世。他的大量信件手稿（超过25,000页）于20世纪60年代入藏大学图书馆。该项目在300年后通过电子版实现其理想，包含全部手稿的全文本转录和图像。1996年和2002年分别出版了CD-ROM版，最新在线版提供免费访问。该项目由谢菲尔德大学人文研究所开发，并由迈克尔·格林格拉斯等人负责。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字档案的价值及其在不同领域的应用

不同观点：
• [peterldowns] 认为数字人文（Digital Humanities）和自然语言处理（NLP）以及更广泛的计算机科学领域（如AI、LLM、GenAI等）之间的交集很少。他指出，数字人文领域主要由图书馆员和档案管理员组成，他们拥有大量有趣的材料，并希望使其更易于访问。他建议，如果有人对这类项目感兴趣，可以直接联系这些专业人士。
  
• [axus] 的评论更关注具体内容，指出档案中的第一个条目以对政府变更的辞职开始，暗示数字档案中具体历史内容的潜在价值和意义。

补充讨论：
• [peterldowns] 强调了跨学科合作的可能性和必要性，特别是数字人文与NLP、AI等领域的合作潜力。
• [axus] 的评论则将焦点转向了数字档案中的具体历史事件和内容，提示了档案在记录历史变迁中的作用。
• 争议的焦点可能在于不同领域对数字档案的关注点不同：一方面是技术与人文的结合，另一方面是档案内容的实际历史和文化价值。

The Hartlib Papers
Home
Search
Search by Reference
Browse the Collections
Search the Hartlib Papers
Keyword or phrase:
Advanced Search
Samuel Hartlib (c1600-62), a great seventeenth-century 'intelligencer' and man of science, set out to record all human knowledge
and make it universally available for the education of all mankind. His correspondence, which runs to over 25,000 folios of
original materials, came to the University Library in the 1960s. The full-text electronic edition realises Hartlib's vision
some 300 years later.
The project's objective was to create a complete electronic edition with full-text transcription and facsimile images of all
25,000 seventeenth-century manuscripts. This seven-year project culminated in the publication in 1996 of two CD-ROMs by University
Microfilms in Michigan. An enlarged edition, incorporating many Hartlib materials from libraries around the world, was published
on CD-ROM by the Humanities Research Institute in July 2002. This new, online edition provides free access to all the content
available on the original CD-ROM versions. Full introductory and background information will be made available shortly.

data.title: The Practical Limitations of End-to-End Encryption
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了关于端到端加密（E2EE）的误解和错误信息，特别是针对特朗普政府误将《大西洋》编辑Jeffrey Goldberg加入讨论也门军事行动的Signal群聊事件。文章澄清了E2EE的真正作用：它确保只有对话参与者能读取信息，保护信息不被通信渠道或网络观察者读取，但不能防止错误添加联系人或确保对话可信。此外，政府和军队由于合规和存档要求，不会使用Signal等应用程序处理机密信息，而是使用专门的安全设施（SCIF）。尽管E2EE在加密上有优势，但它不能解决所有安全问题，特别是在人为错误或政策限制的情况下。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Signal等智能手机应用是否适合用于处理军事或机密信息

不同观点：
• [profmonocle] 认为终端完整性至关重要。如果Apple或Google的系统被攻破，他们可以静默推送更新，将Signal应用替换为将信息转发给敌对方的修改版。任何政府无法完全控制软件部署的系统都不适合处理机密信息。

• [SAI_Peregrinus] 指出Signal的加密技术非常安全，但其用户管理不符合处理军事信息的要求。Signal没有对聊天对象的身份进行验证的功能，也无法检查适当的权限，因此不适合用于军事目的。

• [PaulHoule] 强调了人们在操作安全上的失误。他引用历史事件，如Che Guevara因不当使用一次性密码本而被追踪，说明即使技术安全，人的失误也可能导致安全漏洞。

• [patwolf] 同意智能手机应用如Signal不适合处理机密信息，但对SCIFs（敏感隔离信息设施）作为解决方案提出质疑。认为每次需要通信时都必须进入SCIF是不切实际的。

• [krupan] 认为通过添加条件访问控制（如由可信身份提供者验证用户身份）可以使智能手机应用如Signal适合处理机密信息。这种安全机制已经在许多企业中实现，并可能被商业消息应用支持。

• [perching_aix] 支持使用Matrix等其他通信协议，认为无法解密消息本身即是优势。

• [hypeatei] 提供了一个相关新闻链接，关于特朗普政府意外将战争计划通过短信发给记者，以此引发对信息安全的进一步思考。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于智能手机应用（如Signal）的加密技术是否足够以及其用户管理功能是否符合处理机密信息的要求。
• 有人担心终端完整性和操作安全问题，认为即使技术本身安全，系统性失误和外部攻击仍可能导致信息泄露。
• 关于SCIFs作为解决方案的可行性也被质疑，认为其在实际操作中可能不够灵活。
• 有人提出通过技术改进（如条件访问控制）可以使商业应用适合处理机密信息。

43471223.article_content:
Internet discussions about end-to-end encryption are plagued by misunderstandings, misinformation, and some people totally missing the point.
Of course, people being wrong on the Internet isn’t exactly news.
XKCD: Duty Calls
“What do you want me to do? LEAVE? Then they’ll keep being wrong!”
Yesterday,
a story in
The Atlantic
alleged that the Trump Administration accidentally added their editor, Jeffrey Goldberg, to a Signal group chat discussing a military action in Yemen.
This was quickly confirmed to be authentic.
Brian Hughes, the spokesman for the National Security Council, responded two hours later, confirming the veracity of the Signal group. “This appears to be an authentic message chain, and we are reviewing how an inadvertent number was added to the chain,” Hughes wrote.
The Trump Administration Accidentally Texted Me Its War Plans
— The Atlantic
In the aftermath of this glorious fuck-up by the Trump administration, I have observed many poorly informed hot takes. Some of these were funny, but others are dangerous: they were trying to promote technologies that claim to be
Signal alternatives
, as if this whole story was
somehow
a failure of Signal’s security posture.
Art:
CMYKat
Not to put too fine a point on it: Switching to
Threema
or
PGP
would not have made a lick of difference. Switching to Matrix would have only helped if you consider “unable to decrypt message” helping.
To understand why, you need a clear understanding of what end-to-end encryption is, what it does, what it protects against, and what it doesn’t protect againt.
Towards A Clear Understanding
Imagine for a moment that you decided to build a dedicated, invite-only app that enables you to chat with your friends. For the sake of argument, let’s assume that your friends use multiple devices (computers, smartphones, tablets, one uses a watch, etc.). Despite this, they aren’t always online.
The simplest way to implement such an app requires an architecture that looks like this:
You have an app (or a website) that your friends use to chat with their friends.
If it’s a website, it lives in a browser window.
If it’s an app, it’s installed on their devices.
You have some sort of channel for passing messages between users.
This is often a server that the apps or websites connect to, but you can also setup some sort of peer-to-peer infrastructure.
Any additional requirements only add to the complexity. For example, a consistent message history across devices without storing the message history server-side is actually doable, but requires a bit of careful planning.
What’s End-to-End Encryption?
If you were to take this abstract description of a chat app and add
end-to-end encryption
to it, what you end up doing is
encrypting messages with the app
such that only your friends can decrypt them, using the app on their own devices.
Thus, the “ends” are the software running on each device (also called “endpoints”).
This is in contrast with
transport encryption
(which protects messages between your app and the channel, and also from the channel and your friends’ apps, but
not from the channel itself
) and
at-rest encryption
(which protects messages on your device when you’re not using it).
How Does End-to-End Encryption Improve Security?
End-to-end encryption (E2EE for short) aims to ensure only the participants added to a conversation can read its contents.
The channel that delivers encrypted messages shouldn’t be able to read them.
Other Internet-enabled devices that can observe your network traffic to/from the chat app shouldn’t be able to read them.
What Doesn’t E2EE Give Us?
For one, just because you’re having a private conversation doesn’t mean you’re having a
trustworthy
conversation. An encrypted chat with a scammer will not save you from being scammed.
And as we saw with yesterday’s news story, E2EE also
doesn’t prevent you from accidentally adding an editor for a newspaper to a group chat
.
On Security Clearances and SCIFs
I must be cautious with my wording here, as I have never held a security clearance in my life (and I’ve never aspired to hold one).
Even if a smartphone app was developed tomorrow that successfully boasted better cryptographic security than Signal, it still wouldn’t be an appropriate tool for classified communications for military operations. In fact, I do not foresee any smartphone app ever being approved for this purpose.
Broadly speaking, when politicians describe Signal as a “non-secure” channel, they’re not talking about its cryptographic security at all. Instead, they’re remarking that Signal has not been approved by the US government for this sort of purpose.
Additionally, Signal’s “disappearing messages” feature is fundamentally incompatible with the requirements of governments to preserve documents (even if they’re highly classified).
When government and military officials want to discuss operations, they’re typically required to go into a SCIF (Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility), which ensures:
That

• 有人担心终端完整性和操作安全问题，认为即使技术本身安全，系统性失误和外部攻击仍可能导致信息泄露。
• 关于SCIFs作为解决方案的可行性也被质疑，认为其在实际操作中可能不够灵活。
• 有人提出通过技术改进（如条件访问控制）可以使商业应用适合处理机密信息。

data.article_summary:
这篇文章总结了生物技术和医学领域的几项重要进展：

1. **纳米孔测序**：Asimov Press的Niko McCarty介绍了一种低成本的DNA测序新方法——通过扩展DNA分子（Xpandomers）使其更易读取，提高纳米孔测序的准确性并降低成本。

2. **美国对外援助**：研究显示美国对外援助每年挽救约300万人生命，但特朗普政府取消了90%的USAID合同，包括结核病、母婴健康、HIV治疗等关键项目。

3. **非阿片类止痛药**：FDA批准了Vertex Pharmaceuticals开发的Journavx，它针对NaV1.8蛋白，有效缓解疼痛且不易成瘾，但价格较高。

4. **基孔肯雅疫苗**：FDA批准了Bavarian Nordic的新疫苗，该公司还获得优先审评券，可加快未来药物上市速度。

5. **法医元科学指南**：James Heathers出版了一本关于如何检测学术研究中错误和欺诈的书。

6. **双父小鼠**：中国研究人员通过基因技术使两只雄性小鼠的DNA结合，成功产下后代，但这些小鼠有健康问题且不育。

7. **最大生物AI模型**：Arc Institute推出了Evo 2模型，能预测DNA突变是否致病，准确率超过90%。

8. **学术撤稿问题**：2022年，学术期刊的撤稿率略高于0.2%，其中80%来自Hindawi出版社。

这些进展展示了生物技术和医学领域的最新动态和挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：中国研究人员通过基因技术使两只雄性小鼠的遗传物质产生后代，以及该技术背后的伦理和科学讨论。

不同观点：
• 观点一：该技术具有科学价值。评论者[freedomben]认为这项研究非常有趣，具有突破性。研究展示了通过基因编辑技术，能够让两只雄性小鼠的遗传物质结合，并产生后代，尽管后代存在健康问题和不育。这展示了科学在生殖生物学领域的进步，尤其是在理解性染色体和生殖过程方面的潜力。

• 观点二：技术成功率低，且存在严重的健康问题。研究结果显示，在164次尝试中只有7只小鼠成功出生，且这些小鼠存在严重的健康问题，并终生不育。这表明尽管技术上可行，但其成功率低，且可能导致不健康的个体，因此距离实际应用还有很长的路要走。

• 观点三：伦理争议。虽然评论中未直接提及，但该技术引发了潜在的伦理问题。例如，是否应该在哺乳动物（包括人类）中进行这样的实验，尤其是在后代存在健康问题的情况下。该技术挑战了传统的生殖观念，可能引发关于自然生殖界限的伦理辩论。

补充讨论：
• 该实验中的技术细节，例如如何将雄性小鼠的精子重新编程为干细胞，并通过去除卵子细胞核的方式产生胚胎，显示了当前基因编辑技术在生殖领域的复杂应用。

• 该研究可能对未来同性生殖的研究提供参考，即是否可能通过类似技术实现人类同性伴侣的共同生殖，但目前实验结果显示的技术局限性和伦理问题仍需进一步讨论。

争议焦点：该技术在科学进步和伦理之间的平衡，特别是在实际应用中可能产生的健康问题和伦理挑战。

We recently released Issue 18 of Works in Progress. Read about prehistoric psychopaths, fertility on demand and the king of fruits
here
. Today on Links in Progress
Asimov Press
’s Niko McCarty and our own
Saloni Dattani
return to review more important things happening in the world of biotechnology and medicine.
1. Nanopore sequencing is a promising, low-cost alternative to traditional genome sequencing methods. Nanopores are tiny holes in a membrane. When a molecule passes through a nanopore, it disrupts an electric field. Fluctuations in the field can be ‘decoded’ to figure out whether a passing molecule was an adenine, thymine, or something else. Unfortunately, its use has been limited by poor spatial resolution.
Roche has developed a new sequencing method called
Sequencing by Expansion (SBX)
, which expands DNA molecules into larger polymer structures called Xpandomers and makes them easier to read with nanopores. If successful, SBX would improve the accuracy of nanopore sequencing and bring costs down.
2. Justin Sandefur and Charles Kenny
estimate
that
US foreign aid prevents around 3 million deaths per year at a cost of
only 0.2 percent of the US’s GNI
.
The Trump administration
has scrapped
90 percent of all USAID contracts,
including
some of the most impactful programs. The scrapped contracts seem to include all tuberculosis programs, programs supplying essential medicines for maternal and child health; programs providing HIV treatment; UNICEF’s polio vaccination program; contracts for disease outbreak prevention, detection, and response; emergency food aid; earthquake assistance and more.
3.
The FDA approved a
non-opioid painkiller
.
Journavx, developed by Vertex Pharmaceuticals, targets a protein called the NaV1.8 voltage-gated sodium channel, which transmits pain signals from sensory neurons to the brain. No other drugs on the market target this protein; existing painkillers instead bind to several other different NaV channels at once. In a phase 3 trial with 2,000 patients undergoing surgery, Journavx reduced pain as effectively as hydrocodone plus paracetamol and had fewer side effects. It also does not appear to be addictive. But the drug will cost about $233 per week; opioids cost about $12 per week.
4.
The FDA
approved
a new vaccine for chikungunya
, a mosquito-borne disease that can result in joint pain for months. The new vaccine was developed by Bavarian Nordic, the same company that manufactured the Jynneos Mpox vaccine. Bavarian Nordic have been rewarded for the results of their chikungunya vaccine with a ‘priority disease voucher,’ which will allow them the opportunity to jump the FDA review queue with another drug. Because they primarily affect poorer countries, drugs for curing tropical diseases face a limited financial market. The ‘priority disease voucher’ acts as a reward for Bavarian Nordic, who can use it to
get their next drug to market faster
.
5.
A guide to ‘
forensic metascience
’.
James Heathers, a researcher and scientific sleuth, has published a textbook explaining how to probe academic studies for potential errors, questionable research practices, and scientific fraud.
6.
Chinese researchers made mice with
two genetic fathers
.
They took sperm from male mice and reprogrammed them into stem cells, effectively ‘rewinding’ their development. Those stem cells retained only one set of chromosomes, like normal sperm, but were then fused with a second sperm’s DNA — resulting in both XX and XY sex chromosomes. The resulting DNA was injected into an egg without a nucleus, producing embryos with two paternal genomes. Out of 164 attempts, seven mouse pups were born; they survived to adulthood but had serious health problems and were infertile.
7.
Arc Institute launched the
largest AI model yet
for biology
. Called Evo 2, it was trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides of DNA from 128,000 organisms. Evo 2 can predict whether a given mutation in a DNA sequence will be pathogenic with over 90 percent accuracy, even in instances where scientists have not previously studied that mutation in the laboratory. The model was trained on 2,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs – about 150 times more compute than AlphaFold.
Asimov Press
covered the story
.
8.
In 2022, the retraction rate across hundreds of journals slightly exceeded 0.2 percent, but about 80 percent of these retractions came from journals owned by a single publisher: Hindawi.
This
latest
Nature
report
shows that the problem is pervasive for specific publishers and for select universities. Jining First People’s Hospital had a five percent retraction

data.title: X’s director of engineering, Haofei Wang, has left the company
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: X（前Twitter）的工程主管郝菲·王（Haofei Wang）突然离职。自2021年加入以来，他一直担任公司领导核心，并在马斯克将更多精力转向DOGE和xAI后，实际负责工程和产品事务。他的离职原因不明，公司也未回应置评请求。近期，X引入了新的工程领导层，并与xAI关系日益紧密。尽管马斯克对X的关注减少，但公司估值回升至440亿美元，且仍在开发X Money支付平台。马斯克曾计划将X打造成类似中国微信的全能应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对与Elon Musk相关公司的人员离职和公司发展的不同看法和反应

不同观点：
• [Nckpz的观点] 认为在Elon Musk领导下的公司强调长时间工作和“极度硬核”的工作伦理，长期留在这样的公司可能不健康。该评论暗示公司文化可能过于严苛，不利于员工的长期发展。

• [techpineapple的观点] 则认为员工在科技行业工作三年是一个正常的任期，没有必要对每个员工离职都进行大肆报道。该评论试图淡化对员工离职事件的关注，认为这在行业内是常见现象。

• [only-one1701的观点] 对新闻标题和公司命名表示不满，认为标题有误导性，并且对公司名称表示反感。该评论更多是个人情绪的表达，对媒体报道和公司品牌有批评。

• [anshumankmr的观点] 提到了在使用相关平台时遇到了被错误标记为机器人的问题，导致使用体验很差，最后不得不停止在网页上使用该平台。该评论关注的是产品使用体验问题，并间接批评了公司的技术管理。

• [Oras的观点] 对公司估值在近三年后才回到收购时的水平表示不解，质疑公司在这段时间的增长意义何在。该评论关注的是公司的商业表现和估值问题，认为增长和回报不成正比。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是公司文化的健康程度，尤其是长时间工作和硬核文化对员工的影响。
- 另一个讨论点是公司的人员流动和媒体报道的频率，部分评论认为这是正常现象，无需过度解读。
- 公司估值和增长问题也是一个关键讨论点，有评论对公司经过三年才恢复到收购时的估值表示质疑。
- 最后，用户对平台使用体验的具体问题也有所反馈，反映了公司在技术和用户管理方面可能存在的问题。

X’s head of engineering is out
The sudden departure comes after Musk shifted his attention to DOGE and xAI.
The sudden departure comes after Musk shifted his attention to DOGE and xAI.
by
Kylie Robison
Mar 24, 2025, 7:32 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: The Verge
Kylie Robison
is a senior AI reporter working with The Verge’s policy and tech teams. She previously worked at Fortune Magazine and Business Insider.
X’s director of engineering, Haofei Wang, has suddenly left the company, according to sources with knowledge of the matter.
Wang first joined Elon Musk’s X in July 2021 and has been an integral part of the company’s leadership, often serving as a conduit between Musk and the rest of the company’s engineers. More recently, he was seen internally as X’s defacto head of engineering and product, especially with Musk recently focusing more of his time on xAI and DOGE. It’s unclear why Wang is departing now
.
Neither he nor a company spokesperson responded to a request for comment in time for publication.
X recently added other engineering leadership: Mike Dalton and Uday Ruddaraju, both previously technical leads at Robinhood, joined in January. Their LinkedIn profiles show that they also work at xAI, which has become
increasingly intertwined
with X over the last year.
Do you work at X or xAI?
I’d love to chat. You can reach me securely on Signal @kylie.01 or via email at kylie@theverge.com.
Thanks to the growing profile of xAI and Musk’s newfound political influence, X’s business appears to be turning around. The company reportedly just
obtained a $44 billion valuation
from investors — the same price Musk paid for Twitter in 2022. While Musk remains an avid poster on X, his attention and leadership at X has become increasingly split since he started campaigning for President Donald Trump last summer.
When Musk first purchased Twitter, he vowed to transform it into an “everything app” akin to China’s WeChat.
The Verge
previously reported an internal X meeting
where Musk said that it “would blow my mind” if the company couldn’t handle “someone’s entire financial life” by the end of 2024. Those plans haven’t come to fruition, though my sources say that work is still underway to launch the X Money payments platform (
it’s slated to come
“later this year”).
Update, March 25:
The story was updated to reflect Wang’s start date at Twitter, pre-acquisition and rebrand.

data.title: Critical Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities in Ingress NGINX
data.author: puppion
data.article_summary:
Wiz Research发现了一系列未经身份验证的远程代码执行漏洞（CVE-2025-1097, CVE-2025-1098, CVE-2025-24514, CVE-2025-1974），影响Kubernetes的Ingress NGINX Controller，命名为#IngressNightmare。这些漏洞允许攻击者未经授权访问Kubernetes集群中的所有秘密信息，可能导致集群被接管。该漏洞的CVSS v3.1基础评分高达9.8。

研究显示，约43%的云环境易受此漏洞影响，超过6,500个集群（包括财富500强公司）公开暴露了易受攻击的Ingress控制器。建议尽快修补漏洞。

Ingress NGINX Controller是Kubernetes中常用的入口控制器，默认情况下其 admission controllers 未经身份验证可网络访问，攻击者可利用恶意入口对象实现远程代码执行。

缓解措施包括：
1. 升级到Ingress NGINX Controller的最新版本（1.12.1或1.11.5）。
2. 确保admission webhook端点不外部暴露。
3. 实施严格的网络策略，仅允许Kubernetes API服务器访问admission controller。

可以使用Nuclei模板检查暴露的Ingress-NGINX admission controllers。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kubernetes环境中入口控制器和准入控制器的安全性，尤其是Ingress-NGINX相关漏洞的暴露和利用风险。

不同观点：
• [rollulus] 对Kubernetes准入控制器暴露在公共互联网的情况表示困惑。他认为Kubernetes API虽然暴露在互联网上，但未认证的请求都会被拒绝，因此不理解为何准入控制器会成为问题。他还质疑在什么样的错误配置下，准入控制器会暴露给外界。

• [boxed] 质疑标题中突出NGINX的问题，因为他认为问题出在Kubernetes本身，而不是NGINX。他觉得将问题归咎于NGINX有些不公平。

• [KronisLV] 提到其他入口控制器（如Traefik）并认为碎片化（即有多种不同的入口控制器选择）在一定程度上是好事，因为它限制了单一漏洞大范围影响的可能性。他还指出，使用传统网络服务器（如Caddy或Apache2）作为入口控制器的基础可能对一些长期项目或家庭实验室环境有帮助。

• [SCdF] 提供了一个讨论链接，表示该话题已在其他地方讨论过，但没有深入提出自己的观点。

• [Traubenfuchs] 澄清了漏洞利用的条件，指出要利用此漏洞，攻击者需要直接向Kubernetes资源（准入控制器）发送请求。这种情况通常只有在明显危险的错误配置或极其松散的安全标准下才会发生。正常情况下，Kubernetes资源不应从互联网访问。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于准入控制器的暴露和利用风险，以及问题是否应归咎于NGINX。
• 讨论中还涉及到Kubernetes集群的安全配置问题，特别是如何避免将Kubernetes资源暴露在公共互联网中。
• [KronisLV] 提出了对入口控制器多样性的看法，认为多样性可以减少单一漏洞的广泛影响，但也担心许多用户可能不会及时更新或修复不安全的软件配置。

总结：评论主要围绕Kubernetes准入控制器的安全性、错误配置的可能性以及问题是否应归因于NGINX展开讨论。参与者对漏洞利用的具体条件和配置错误的影响有不同理解，并探讨了可能的解决方案和安全实践。

Wiz Research discovered CVE-2025-1097, CVE-2025-1098, CVE-2025-24514 and CVE-2025-1974, a series of unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerabilities in Ingress NGINX Controller for Kubernetes dubbed
#IngressNightmare
. Exploitation of these vulnerabilities leads to unauthorized access to all secrets stored across all namespaces in the Kubernetes cluster by attackers, which can result in cluster takeover.
This attack vector has been assigned a CVSS v3.1 base score of 9.8.
In this blog post, we share key learnings from our discovery of
IngressNightmare
, affecting the admission controller component of Ingress NGINX Controller for Kubernetes. Based on our analysis, about 43% of cloud environments are vulnerable to these vulnerabilities, with our research uncovering over 6,500 clusters, including Fortune 500 companies, that publicly expose vulnerable Kubernetes ingress controllers’ admission controllers to the public internet—putting them at immediate critical risk.
We recommend patching as soon as possible. This blog post details the technical elements of the vulnerability and contains mitigation and detection guidance for defenders.
We would like to thank the Ingress-NGINX maintainers, particularly
Marco Ebert
, for their help in addressing the IngressNightmare vulnerabilities. Our team worked closely with the Kubernetes maintainers and security teams to ensure this attack surface was fully eliminated before public disclosure. Kubernetes’s blog can be found
here
, and
Amazon
and
Google Cloud
have also published their own advisories.
What is Ingress NGINX Controller for Kubernetes?
Ingress NGINX Controller is one of the most popular
ingress controllers
available for Kubernetes, and a core Kubernetes project, with over 18,000 stars on
GitHub
. Using Ingress-NGINX is one of the most common methods for exposing Kubernetes applications externally. As an ingress controller, its job is to accept incoming traffic and route it to the relevant Kubernetes Services, which in turn forwards the traffic to the appropriate Pods, based on a set of rules. Specifically, Ingress NGINX Controller is based on the popular
NGINX reverse proxy
.
Figure: Ingress prerequisites from the Kubernetes documentation.
Ingress-NGINX is explicitly highlighted in the Kubernetes documentation as an example Ingress controller that fulfills the prerequisite for using Ingress in Kubernetes. Our research show that over 41% of internet-facing clusters are running Ingress-NGINX.
The Vulnerability
Ingress NGINX deploys an admission controller within its pod, designed to validate incoming ingress objects before they are deployed. By default, admission controllers are accessible over the network without authentication, making them a highly appealing attack vector.
When the Ingress-NGINX admission controller processes an incoming ingress object, it constructs an NGINX configuration from it and then validates it using the NGINX binary.  Our team found a vulnerability in this phase that allows injecting an arbitrary NGINX configuration remotely, by sending a malicious ingress object directly to the admission controller through the network.
During the configuration validation phase, the injected NGINX configuration causes the NGINX validator to execute code, allowing remote code execution (RCE) on the Ingress NGINX Controller’s pod.
The admission controller’s elevated privileges and unrestricted network accessibility create a critical escalation path. Exploiting this flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code and access all cluster secrets across namespaces, that could lead to complete cluster takeover.
Figure: IngressNightmare attack vectors
To be clear, gaining initial access to a cluster's pod network is not as difficult as one might think - containerization on its own is not a strong security boundary, and many applications running on K8s are susceptible to container escape, as we have repeatedly demonstrated in our research of cloud and SaaS applications over the past few years. Additionally, these vulnerabilities pair very well with SSRF vulnerabilities, which are an arguably common occurrence in web applications.
Mitigation & Detection
First, determine if your clusters are using ingress-nginx. In most cases, you can check this by running
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --selector app.kubernetes.io/name=ingress-nginx
with (at least) cluster-scoped read-only permissions.
This vulnerability is fixed in Ingress NGINX Controller
version 1.12.1 and 1.11.5
. We strongly recommend that cluster admins:
Update to the latest version
of Ingress NGINX Controller.
Ensure
the admission webhook endpoint is
not exposed externally
.
You can use this
Nuclei template
to check for exposed Ingress-NGINX admission controllers.
If you can’t upgrade immediately, consider one of these mitigations:
Enforce strict network policies
so only the Kubernetes API Server can access the admission controller.
Temporarily disable
the admissio

data.title: A sodium-ion portable power bank comes to market
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary: Elecom推出了一款采用钠离子电池的Na Plus充电宝，该产品不使用锂，可在极端温度下使用，并可充电近5000次。其9000mAh容量具备45W的USB-C输出和18W的USB-A输出，充电需约两小时。虽然钠离子电池更环保且 safer，但其能量密度较低，导致体积和重量较大。目前该产品在日本售价9980日元（约67美元），初期产能和生产规模有限。尽管体积大且价格高，但钠离子技术在环保和安全性方面具有潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：钠离子电池的潜力和局限

不同观点：
• **不看好钠离子电池的未来**：[torginus] 认为钠离子电池的未来不乐观。他指出，钠离子比锂离子大三倍，储存相同电量时更重，且会对电池分离器造成更大损伤，导致循环次数降低。此外，锂离子电池的价格已经下降，不再是成本的主要驱动因素，因此不值得看好钠离子电池。

• **钠离子电池的优化潜力**：[ldoughty] 关注钠离子电池的重量和体积问题，质疑这是否可以通过技术进步得到改善，或者仅仅是密度的固有局限。他提到，目前钠离子电池需要多75%的空间来提供相同的功率，并询问未来是否能达到锂离子电池的密度和尺寸水平，或者是否会遇到瓶颈。

• **钠离子电池的优势和应用场景**：[jauntywundrkind] 强调钠离子电池的优势，如宽温度范围（-30至122华氏度），高循环次数（5000次，类似于LFP），以及高安全性和高电流性能。他将其性能与LFP和Li-Po电池进行比较，指出钠离子电池在某些方面表现接近LFP，并期待获得更精确的能量密度数据。

• **实际应用和市场潜力**：[aitchnyu] 关注钠离子电池在实际应用中的可能性，如在高温环境下使用的行车记录仪电池。[1970-01-01] 则看好钠离子电池在电动滑板车和电动自行车市场的潜力，认为其具备便宜、安全和可靠的优势，并预期随着量产成熟，其尺寸会进一步缩小。

补充讨论：
• **温度适应性和安全性**：钠离子电池在温度适应性和安全性方面的优势被多次提及，特别是在高温环境下的表现和较高的循环次数。

• **市场应用前景**：部分评论者看好钠离子电池在特定市场（如电动滑板车和电动自行车）的应用，认为其低成本和可靠性是关键优势。

争议焦点：钠离子电池的能量密度和重量问题是否能够通过技术进步得到显著改善，从而在更多应用场景中与锂离子电池竞争。

Accessory maker Elecom has
announced what it’s claiming to be
the first consumer-ready power bank that uses a sodium-ion battery instead of a lithium-ion one,
as spotted by
Notebookcheck
. In addition to being
more environmentally friendly
to manufacture, the 9,000mAh Na Plus can be used in extreme temperatures with less risk of overheating, and has — Elecom claims — a lifespan of almost 5,000 charges. Even if you’re recharging it every single day, after 13 years it should still be providing power.
Sodium-ion battery technology is new compared to lithium-ion tech, and production capacities haven’t reached the level of lithium-ion batteries. So while a little deal-hunting can get you a basic 10,000mAh lithium-ion power bank from
companies like Anker for less than $20
, the
Na Plus is debuting in Japan
(in black and light gray color options) for 9,980 yen, or around $67. Elecom hasn’t yet announced a wider rollout.
The Elecom Na Plus offers basic power bank functionality with a single USB-C and USB-A port.
Image: Elecom
Power output maxes out at 45W through a single USB-C port, or 18W through the Na Plus’ lone USB-A port. A series of LEDs can be used to determine the power bank’s remaining power level, and it takes about two hours to fully charge it.
Performance-wise, the Na Plus definitely isn’t the most capable portable charger you can buy. What’s inside is what’s most exciting. Although lithium-ion technology has dominated batteries since the early ‘90s, lithium isn’t an unlimited resource, and mining it (as well as other metals used in batteries like cobalt and nickel) involves energy-intensive processes that can pollute local ecosystems.
Sodium-ion batteries — like the name might suggest — function similarly to lithium-ion ones, but with sodium instead of lithium. Sodium is more abundantly available and much easier to produce. Sodium-ion batteries are also safer to use. Elecom says the Na Plus can operate in temperatures ranging from around -30 to 122 degrees Fahrenheit and is at less risk of fires caused by overheating and thermal runaway.
The price tag on this technology might drop in the future as the supply chain expands and production increases. But doing those things likely won’t solve this other drawback: sodium-ion batteries are simply bigger all around. These batteries have a lower energy density compared to lithium-based batteries, meaning they have to be larger and heavier to store an equivalent amount of energy. Case in point: that 10,000mAh lithium battery from Anker weighs around 213 grams, while the 9,000mAh Na Plus is 350 grams and much bulkier.
Sodium-ion batteries might be better suited for applications where size isn’t the primary concern, such as storage systems for renewable energy sources, backup power supplies, or powering vehicles like cargo ships. The Na Plus might be bulky and expensive, but it’s still exciting to see this technology finally reach consumers.
